entries.label: 17-string bass koto
entries.gloss: A koto with 17 rather than 13 strings, sometimes described as a bass koto.

entries.label: Anglo concertina
entries.gloss: Bisonoric and button layout like the German, reeds and hexagonal ends like the english, this concertina was created to rival the popular German variant imported into England.

entries.label: Appalachian dulcimer
entries.gloss: Historically a folk instrument from Appalachia, its elongated figure-of-eight shaped soundbox is made of various woods and often has heart-shaped sound-holes. It has 3 to 4 metal strings (including drone) and is fretted diatonically.

entries.label: Baltic psalteries
entries.gloss: Family of related plucked box-zithers from the Baltic area, each hold a strong traditional significance within their respective communities Members include: * Kantele from Finland * Kannel from Estland * Kanklės from Lithuania * Kokles from Latvia * Gusli from Russia/Belarus Additional members include the Russian Mari-people's Kusle, the Latvian Livonian-people's Kāndla and the Sápmi Harpu.

entries.label: Batá drum
entries.gloss: Primarily in the religious rituals of the Yoruba and diaspora, these hourglass shaped drums have membranes on each end. Their names are largest to least: Iyá, Itótele, Okónkolo.

entries.label: Blaster Beam
entries.gloss: Very long metal bar fitted with strings and electric pickups, it makes a deep ominous booming sound and is often used in score.

entries.label: Cembalet
entries.gloss: Electromechanical piano with stainless steel reeds and an amplified pick-up. Not to be confused with "cembalo" which is another name for Harpsichord.

entries.label: Cretan lyra
entries.gloss: The Cretan lyra is a Greek pear-shaped, three-stringed bowed musical instrument, central to the traditional music of Crete and parts of Greece.

entries.label: E-flat clarinet
entries.gloss: The E♭ clarinet is a member of the clarinet family.

entries.label: EWI
entries.gloss: EWI (an acronym for electric wind instrument) is the name of Akai's wind controller.

entries.label: English concertina
entries.gloss: Unisonoric concertina with hexagonal sides and concertina reeds.

entries.label: English flageolet
entries.gloss: Meant as an improvement on the flageolet design, the English flageolet had six finger holes in the front and one thumb hole in the back.

entries.label: German concertina
entries.gloss: More usually square than hexagonal, with long plate reeds.

entries.label: German harp
entries.gloss: German/Bohemian harp

entries.label: Gravikord
entries.gloss: Based on the polyrhythm of the Afrikan kora, kalimba and Japanese koto, it is electro-acoustic with a stainless steel frame with 24 nylon strings and an integral piezoelectric sensor.

entries.label: Great Highland bagpipe
entries.gloss: Known since 1400, traditionally in military context, today it is the most widespread and famous of bagpipes.

entries.label: Guitaret
entries.gloss: Small white electric thumb piano with metal tines and an electromagnetic pickup.

entries.label: Indonesian rebab
entries.gloss: Introduced to Indonesia in the 15th century, this variant of the spike-fiddle rebab has two bowed metal strings with characteristically long tuning pegs and is made of hide-covered wood or coconut shell. It is the melody leader in gamelan and is also used in healing rituals.

entries.label: Irish flute
entries.gloss: Wooden flute of the simple-system type, popular in Irish folk music.

entries.label: Irish harp / clàrsach
entries.gloss: An Irish/Scottish harp.

entries.label: Lyricon
entries.gloss: The Lyricon is an electronic wind instrument.

entries.label: Magyar duda
entries.gloss: Used by shepherds and in pagan lifestyle, it has a double bore chanter with one to 2 drones, historically made of dogskin but today goat is used.

entries.label: Mark tree
entries.gloss:
Solid metal (often aluminium) rods hanging on a bar, set at an inharmonic pitch.
NOT to be confused with the standalone glockenspiel-like chime bar(s).

entries.label: Marxophone
entries.gloss: A type of fretless zither.

entries.label: Mexican vihuela
entries.gloss: Mexican vihuela, used by mariachi bands.

entries.label: Northumbrian pipes
entries.gloss: Used for more than 250 years, its one chanter and usually four drones have narrow bores.

entries.label: Otamatone
entries.gloss: Shaped like an eighth-note with a cute face, it is played with one hand fingering the neck and the other squeezing the head to create wavering sound.

entries.label: Paraguayan harp
entries.gloss: The Paraguayan harp is a 32-48-string diatonic harp used in Paraguay and Venezuela.

entries.label: Pianet
entries.gloss: Electromechanical piano (not to be confused with electronic piano) designed and produced by Hohner in the 1960 and 70s.

entries.label: Pierrot ensemble
entries.gloss: Chamber ensemble of five players (flute, clarinet, violin, cello and piano). Originally required for Schönberg's Pierrot Lunaire, it became a fairly common combination for 20th century classical groups.

entries.label: Portuguese guitar
entries.gloss: Used in fado, it has twelve steel strings, strung in six courses.

entries.label: Radhika's Mohan veena
entries.gloss:
For the modified slide-guitar created in the 1990's by Vishwa Mohan Bhatt see Bhatt's Mohan veena.
Created as a modified sarod by Radhika Maitra in the 1940s, it has a wooden soundbox cover (like sitar), an extra neck resonator (like veena) and the fretboard from the sarod.

entries.label: Reactable
entries.gloss: The Reactable is an electronic musical instrument consisting of a round translucent table on which blocks are placed.

entries.label: Rhodes piano
entries.gloss: Electric keyboard tuning fork idiophone

entries.label: Saraswati veena
entries.gloss: Used in Carnatic tradition, named after goddess of art and music Saraswati, it is known since ancient times. Lute with a gourd sound resonator, it has 24 fixed frets, 7 steel strings (4 main & 3 drone).

entries.label: Schwyzerörgeli
entries.gloss: The Schwyzerörgeli is a type of diatonic button accordion used in Swiss folk music.

entries.label: Scottish smallpipes
entries.gloss: Like (and developed from) the Northumbrian smallpipes, but with Great Highland Bagpipe fingering.

entries.label: Stroh violin
entries.gloss: Instead of a wooden body, it is amplified by a metal horn resonator; its louder and more directional sound made it useful in loud areas.

entries.label: The Great Stalacpipe Organ
entries.gloss: Located in the Luray Caverns of Virginia USA, it is made of an electric console wired to mallets striking thirty-seven stalactites producing tones. This is a singular specific instrument, not an instrument type.

entries.label: Tonette
entries.gloss: introduced in 1938, it was a popular American educational instrument.

entries.label: VM Bhatt's Mohan veena
entries.gloss:
For the modified sarod created in the 1940's by Radhika Mohan Maitra see Radhika's Mohan veena.
Created as a modified Hawaiian or lapsteel guitar, it has 19 to 21 strings and a gourd added to the neck.

entries.label: Vietnamese guitar
entries.gloss: The Vietnamese guitar is similar to a normal guitar, but with scalloped fingerboard resulting in elevated frets similar to the đàn nguyệt.

entries.label: Wiener Horn
entries.gloss: Used in classical and orchestral music, mostly by orchestras in Vienna.

entries.label: Wurlitzer electric piano
entries.gloss: The Wurlitzer electric piano is an electric piano where flat steel reeds are struck by felt hammers.

entries.label: Xaphoon
entries.gloss: The Xaphoon is a keyless chromatic single-reed woodwind instrument.

entries.label: accordina
entries.gloss: Harmonica/accordion hybrid where the bellows for the accordion bit with buttons/keys receive air though the user blowing into the instrument like an harmonica.

entries.label: accordion
entries.gloss: Invented and developed by several people in the early 1800's, it has an arm operated bellows with keys or buttons at one end and bass buttons at the other.

entries.label: acoustic fretless guitar
entries.gloss: Acoustic guitar without frets.

entries.label: afoxé
entries.gloss: Made of a gourd wrapped in a beaded net, it is used in Brazilian afoxé music.

entries.label: agogô
entries.gloss: Originating in West Africa, it consists of (usually) two differing pitch metal bells, it is used in various Brazilian samba music.

entries.label: ajaeng
entries.gloss: The ajaeng is a bowed Korean zither with 7 (sometimes 8 or 9) strings.

entries.label: akete
entries.gloss: Three-parts drumset (baandu, funde and kete) commonly used in Burru and Nyabinghi musics.

entries.label: akkordolia
entries.gloss: Similar to the Japanese taishogoto, it has an elongated teardrop shaped wooden body with button accordion like keys which plays the melody and sets chords.

entries.label: alfaia
entries.gloss: The alfaia is a Brazilian cylindrical drum.

entries.label: algozey
entries.gloss: The algozey is a wooden, beaked double-flute traditionally played by goat herders in the Punjab region of India and Pakistan.

entries.label: alphorn
entries.gloss: The alphorn, or alpine horn, is a conical wood horn used for communication in mountains.

entries.label: alto clarinet
entries.gloss: The alto clarinet is a clarinet in E♭ or sometimes F, normally with a curved neck.

entries.label: alto flute
entries.gloss: The alto flute is a concert flute in G, lower in tone than the flûte d'amour.

entries.label: alto saxophone
entries.gloss: The most common member of the saxophone family, it is the alto member.

entries.label: alto viol
entries.gloss: Alt, alto or contralto member of the viol family. Not to be confused with the Viola of the violin family, known as "Alto" in French.

entries.label: amadinda
entries.gloss: Southern Ugandan giant xylophone, made on with resonating hardwood bars.

entries.label: aman khuur
entries.gloss: Mongolian mouth harp. There are two types: temür/tömör khuur (steel) and khulsan khuur (bamboo).

entries.label: analog synthesizer
entries.gloss: Using analogue circuits and techniques to produce sound electronically, the first types where created in the 1920's with thermionic valves and other electromechanical machineries.

entries.label: angklung
entries.gloss: Usually consisting of 2-3 carved bamboo tubes suspended in a wooden or bamboo frame that is shook. It has been in use since ancient times by Sundanese peoples.

entries.label: antara
entries.gloss: Used in traditional Andes music, it consists of a single row of pipes.

entries.label: anvil
entries.gloss: Originally used just by blacksmiths, the crisp, clear tone produced was noticed by even early composers. In modern use, it is specifically made for music from tuned metal, sometimes placed in a resonator, and is struck with metal hammers.

entries.label: archlute
entries.gloss: The archlute is a European plucked string instrument developed around 1600 as a compromise between the very large theorbo and the Renaissance tenor lute.

entries.label: archtop guitar
entries.gloss: An archtop guitar is a steel-stringed acoustic or semi-acoustic guitar with a distinctive arched top, which is particularly popular with jazz players.

entries.label: arghul
entries.gloss: The arghul is a traditional Egyptian double-pipe, single-reed woodwind instrument.

entries.label: arpeggione
entries.gloss: Invented in 1823, it had a body like a medieval fiddle, but had frets and tuning like the guitar.

entries.label: arrabel
entries.gloss: Scraper made of bones tied together with rope scraped with a conch-shell, in Catalonia it's scraped with a castanet. Ginebra is a variant made of cane.

entries.label: ashiko
entries.gloss: conical goatskin frame-drum originating with the Yoruba people of West Africa, it is also found in Afro-Caribbean and Afro-Latin American cultures.

entries.label: atabaque
entries.gloss: The atabaque is a tall Brazilian hand drum.

entries.label: atarigane
entries.gloss: The atarigane is a Japanese gong which is struck using a deer horn mallet.

entries.label: autoharp
entries.gloss: Initially developed in 1880's by Gütter, it was produced and sold by Zimmerman in America and became popular in the 1910 and onward. Wooden box zither has spring mounted bars used to mute strings for chords.

entries.label: baandu
entries.gloss: Larger bass drum also known as thunder or pope smasher, it has a double goat skin membrane and is hit with a padded mallet. Important in the Jamaican Burru music and Rastafari movement, it is part of the Nyabinghi/Akete drums.

entries.label: baglamas
entries.gloss: Long necked bowl lute, it is named after a related Turkish lute.

entries.label: bagpipe
entries.gloss: The bagpipe is an instrument consisting of a series of enclosed reeds fed by a bag of air.

entries.label: bajo sexto
entries.gloss: Mexican 6 course 12 string bass

entries.label: balafon
entries.gloss: West African xylophone that uses gourds as its resonators.

entries.label: bandoneón
entries.gloss: Invented and used in 1800's Europe, it became popular in Argentina. Unlike concertinas it is square, but alike its button action is parallel, typically it has several reeds per button.

entries.label: bandora
entries.gloss: Although originally built like a cittern, its 6-7 courses of strings were tuned more like a lute.

entries.label: bandura
entries.gloss: Large box lute-zither with a short, unfretted neck. It has 30 or more strings fanned out on the body, the four to eight bass strings are strung to the neck.

entries.label: bangu
entries.gloss: Widely used in folk music, opera and music ensembles, it can be round or cone-shaped with cow/pigskin nailed to the larger convex end which has a small hole (guxin).

entries.label: banhu
entries.gloss: The banhu is a Chinese bowed string instrument in the huqin family. It is also called banghu for its use in bangzi opera.

entries.label: banjitar
entries.gloss: The banjitar is a six-string banjo with the neck of a guitar.

entries.label: banjo-ukulele
entries.gloss: Small fretted hybrid instrument with a banjo body and a ukulele neck, popular in the 1920-30.

entries.label: banjolin
entries.gloss: Reinvented several times in different lands, it combines banjo body and neck of mandolin, it is tuned like it and the violin.

entries.label: bansuri
entries.gloss: The bansuri is a transverse alto flute, which is the North Indian counterpart to the venu.

entries.label: barbat
entries.gloss: Ancient Central Asian/Persian string instrument, ancestor of the Iranian oud. it was an important instrument in pre-Islamic Iran and Persia. The current “Persian barbat” is more similar to the oud.

entries.label: baritone horn
entries.gloss: The baritone horn is a piston valve brass instrument with a wide-rimmed cup mouthpiece which is pitched in B♭, one octave below the B♭ trumpet.

entries.label: baritone saxophone
entries.gloss: The most common of the lower members of the saxophone family, it is the middle-low baritone.

entries.label: baroque guitar
entries.gloss: Predecessor of the modern classical guitar, it had gut strings and even gut frets. First described in 1555, it surpassed the Renaissance lute's popularity.

entries.label: baroque rackett
entries.gloss: Improved by Johann Christoph Denner sometime around 1730, its "coiled snake" bore now is conical, in addition it is played through a removable metal curled mouth piece.

entries.label: baroque trumpet
entries.gloss: Based on the natural trumpet used in the 1500s to 1700s, this mid 20th century reinvention lacks valves but may have vents.

entries.label: barrel organ
entries.gloss: A barrel organ is a mechanical musical instrument typically operated by a person turning a crank which turns a barrel which has music encoded onto it.

entries.label: baryton
entries.gloss: Hybrid between the viol and the bandora, it has an extra set of plucked strings in addition to the bowed ones. Used regularly in Europe until the end of the 18th century.

entries.label: bass
entries.gloss: Bass is a common but generic credit which refers to more than one instrument, the most common being the bass guitar and the double bass (a.k.a. contrabass, acoustic upright bass, wood bass). Please use the correct instrument if you know which one is intended.

entries.label: bass clarinet
entries.gloss: The bass clarinet is a clarinet, typically pitched an octave below the soprano B♭ clarinet.

entries.label: bass flute
entries.gloss: The bass flute is a flute, pitched one octave below the C concert flute, with a tube about 1.5 meters long.

entries.label: bass harmonica
entries.gloss: The bass harmonica is a type of octave harmonica where the lowest note (E) is the same as that on a bass guitar.

entries.label: bass oboe
entries.gloss: The bass oboe is a double reed woodwind instrument which is about twice the size of a regular oboe.

entries.label: bass saxophone
entries.gloss: Second largest and lowest member of the saxophone family. It is similar to the baritone, but larger and with a longer loop near the mouthpiece.

entries.label: bass synthesizer
entries.gloss: A bass synthesizer is used to create sounds in the bass range.

entries.label: bass viol
entries.gloss: Most common viol member today, it was the bass-range viol in the original consort.

entries.label: bass violin
entries.gloss: Sixteenth century predecessor of the violoncello, it was fretless with f-holes and had at first three, then later four, strings tuned in fifths.

entries.label: bateria
entries.gloss: Used in Brazilian samba schools and to accompany capoeira, ensemble consists of various mostly percussion instruments.

entries.label: bawu
entries.gloss: The bawu is a Chinese wind instrument. Although shaped like a flute, it is actually a free reed instrument, with a single metal reed. It is played in a transverse (horizontal) manner.

entries.label: bazooka
entries.gloss:
Not to be confused with the bouzouki.
Large wide tube with a very strongly flaring bell, the telescoping creates only subtle fluctuating overtones. It inspired the name of the anti-tank weapon.

entries.label: bedug
entries.gloss: Extra large double-headed water buffalo hide barrel drum. It is suspended from a rack and beat with mallet, it is used in central Javanese gamelan and for religious signalling purposes in mosques.

entries.label: bell
entries.gloss: Cup or bellshaped bells, these are shook or struck.

entries.label: bell plate
entries.gloss: Used occasionally in the western classical orchestra and theatre, it consists of several tuned aluminium, steel or bronze plates, struck to imitate the sound of bells.

entries.label: bell tree
entries.gloss: A bell tree is a percussion instrument, consisting of vertically nested inverted metal bowls.

entries.label: bellowed reed
entries.gloss: Free reeds with bellows attached, often in a square shape, thence called squeezebox.

entries.label: bendir
entries.gloss: Bendir, frame drum from North Africa, doesn't have jingles.

entries.label: berda
entries.gloss: Bass member of the Serbo-Croatian tamburica orchestra, it is contrabass like. It has four thick metal strings.

entries.label: bhapang
entries.gloss: Originating in Mewati community of Rahajastan, India, it is traditionally made of gourd with top and bottom cut off, with a goat hide membrane nailed to one opening and a gut string which ends in a bamboo piece attached to the membrane. The instrument is held in the armpit and played by plucking the string while pulling it.

entries.label: bicycle bell
entries.gloss: Bell as found on bicycles, sound is made by internal spring loaded hammer, not unlike alarm-clock.

entries.label: bin-sasara
entries.gloss: The binzasara is a Japanese percussion instrument made of many small slats of wood connected by a spine of string with handles at each end.

entries.label: bin-sitar
entries.gloss: Hybrid fretted stick-zither

entries.label: biniou
entries.gloss: Developed from the veuze and often accompanying the bombard, the small high-pitched, singular octave bagpipe is used in Breton folk dancing.

entries.label: birch lur
entries.gloss: Known from the Viking age, this natural brass trumpet/horn was made of wood or birch bark.

entries.label: bisernica
entries.gloss: Smallest member of the Serbo-Croatian tamburica orchestra, it is usually the lead or "prim" instrument. It can either have one double string and three single strings (prim/bisernica) or two double strings and two single strings (bisernica).

entries.label: biwa
entries.gloss: The biwa is a short-necked Japanese fretted lute which is played with a large triangular-shaped plectrum.

entries.label: body percussion
entries.gloss: Percussion performed by parts of the body.

entries.label: bolon
entries.gloss: The bolon is a traditional harp-lute played in several African countries.

entries.label: bombarde
entries.gloss: Conical bore double-reed musical instrument from Brittany.

entries.label: bombo legüero
entries.gloss: Used in folklore music of Andes, it is a descendant of European bass drum. It has a shoulder strap and two soft headed mallets used to strike the goat or llama pelt membrane.

entries.label: bonang
entries.gloss: Consisting of bossed bronze kettle-like gongs arranged in elaborately decorated wooden frames, these are hit with tabuh beaters.

entries.label: bonang barung
entries.gloss: One to two octaves below panerus, it plays elaborate melodies and is one of the most important instruments in the ensemble.

entries.label: bonang panembung
entries.gloss: Chiefly used in Yogyvanese gamelan, the largest and deepest pitched member of the bonang family of gong-chimes.

entries.label: bonang panerus
entries.gloss: Used to play fast melodies, it is the highest pitched member of the bonang family of gong-chimes.

entries.label: bones
entries.gloss: Made of bone or wood, these are paired sticks of sonorous material used in folk music.

entries.label: boobam
entries.gloss: Pipes of bamboo with goat or calfskin membranes, the pitches depend largely on tube-lenght, it is the ancestor to the octoban. Modern variants are usually made of wood, plastic or metal with plastic membranes.

entries.label: boomwhacker
entries.gloss: Often used in group musical education and by street musicians, it consists of individual colourful hollow plastic tubes of various widths that are struck on various surfaces to produce sound, tubes can also be arranged and hit by mallets.

entries.label: bouzar / gouzouki
entries.gloss: Guitar-bouzouki hybrid with guitar body and 4 pairs of strings like the bouzouki, developed separately several different luthiers, among them Stefan Sobell (bouzar) and Davy Stuart (gouzouki).

entries.label: bowed piano
entries.gloss: A piano whose strings are bowed, using nylon filament or other materials.

entries.label: brač
entries.gloss: Second smallest member of the Serbo-Croatian tamburica orchestra, there are often two, first and second bass. It can either have three double strings or two double strings and three single strings.

entries.label: bronze lur
entries.gloss: Chiefly Scandinavian, these bronze age natural brass horns were ritualistically buried in pairs.

entries.label: bugarija
entries.gloss: Chord rhythm member of the Serbo-Croatian tamburica orchestra, it is guitar like. It has one double string D and three single strings.

entries.label: buisine
entries.gloss: The buisine was a type of straight medieval trumpet usually made of metal.

entries.label: buk
entries.gloss: The buk is a Korean drum. While buk is a generic term for drum, it normally refers to a shallow barrel-shaped drum with a wooden body.

entries.label: bulbul tarang
entries.gloss: Developed from the Japanese taishogoto, it is made of wood, often an integral case. It has two courses of strings; drone and melody strings operated by buttons or keys.

entries.label: bīn
entries.gloss:
One of the two subfamilies of Indian chordophones, the North Indian stick zither used in classical Hindustani music has two (or more) large gourd sound resonators and a stick or tube body.
Commonly called "bin", "been" or "bean", the representative is rudra veena, and credits to just "bin" are usually that.

entries.label: cabasa
entries.gloss: Developed from the African agbe, a small shaker not unlike shekere, it is made of wood and metal, with metal beads.

entries.label: cabrette
entries.gloss:
Not to be confused with chabrette, a Limousin bagpipe.
19th century Auvergne goat-skin based bag with double reed chanter and purely decorative drone in single stock.
Early models were mouth blown, later modified to have bellows.

entries.label: caixa
entries.gloss: Traditionally used in samba and maracatu, it originates from the European military battalion. It is made of a 30-35 cm diameter metal barrel strung with a synthetic material, upon which a steel wire or guitar string is strung across.

entries.label: cajón
entries.gloss: Cajón, Peruvian box drum

entries.label: calabash
entries.gloss: Made of dried gourd. Struck with hands or objects.

entries.label: calung
entries.gloss:
Made of multiple vertical hung bamboo tubes with segments cut out to create different pitch. They can be played either hanging suspended or on a bamboo frame like a xylophone.
For the Balinese metallophone sometimes known as chalung or calung, see jublag.

entries.label: castanets
entries.gloss: Pair of concave wood, bone, shell or even fibreglass shells, they are combined by a string and are often used by dancers.

entries.label: cavaquinho
entries.gloss: Small Portuguese lute with four wire or gut strings, it has many descendants in South and Latin America.

entries.label: celesta
entries.gloss: Similar to how a piano works, here keys operate hammers that strike metal plates, creating a soft bell sound.

entries.label: cello
entries.gloss: Also know as violoncello (the "small large viol"), it is the medium bass member of the modern violin family and a principal member of the symphony orchestra.

entries.label: chacha
entries.gloss: Chacha, west Indian rattle

entries.label: chakhe
entries.gloss: The chakhe is a three stringed crocodile shaped plucked zither from Thailand.

entries.label: chalumeau
entries.gloss:
For the Japanese descendant named from Portuguese, see charumera.
For the medieval double-reed woodwind see shawm.
Predecessor of the modern clarinet, 7-regular 1-thumb holed single-reed woodwind was in use during baroque and classical era.

entries.label: chamber organ
entries.gloss: A chamber organ is a small pipe organ.

entries.label: chamberlin
entries.gloss: electromechanical piano

entries.label: chande
entries.gloss: The chande is a drum used in the traditional and classical music of South India.

entries.label: chanzy
entries.gloss: The chanzy is a three-stringed Tuvan lute.

entries.label: chap
entries.gloss: Chap are a pair of cymbals used in Thai and Cambodian music. They are larger, flatter and thinner than the cymbals known as ching.

entries.label: charango
entries.gloss: Used by the Quechua and Aymara, it is a small lute of 5 courses with 10 strings.

entries.label: charumera
entries.gloss:
For the similarly named single-reed woodwind see chalumeau.
For the European instrument, see shawm.
Name derived from the Portuguese name of shawm, it was imported by Iberian traders. It is used in kabuki theatre and by ramen street vendors.

entries.label: chau gong
entries.gloss: The chau gong is a large gong made of brass or bronze which is almost flat except for the rim.

entries.label: chikuzen biwa
entries.gloss: The chikuzen biwa is a biwa with either four strings and frets or five strings and frets popularised during the Meiji period.

entries.label: chime bar
entries.gloss:
Despite the name, it is not a chime but instead consists of tuned metal bars each on individual resonator boxes.
It is similar to glockenspiel.
For the instrument called bar chimes, see chimes.

entries.label: chirimía
entries.gloss: A relative of the shawm, it was introduced to central and south-america by the Spanish in the sixteenth and seventeenth century.

entries.label: chirimía and drum
entries.gloss: Much like the pipe and tabor, the chirimía and drum is a South American cousin.

entries.label: chitarra battente
entries.gloss: Developed chiefly as a folk instrument for accompanying singing and dancing, its front has a intricately carved soundhole and slants towards the bottom where the 5 double (sometimes triple courses) of thin steel strings are fastened with pins. The back can be rounded or flat.

entries.label: chitra veena
entries.gloss: 13th century or earlier South Indian fretless slide lute used in Carnatic music. Hollow body made of jack-fruit with a secondary resonator of hollowed out gourd, it has 6 main, 3 drone and 11-12 sympathetic strings with a sliding block of hardwood to vary pitch. Much like the North Indian vichitra veena is to the rudra veena, chitra veena is to the Saraswati veena.

entries.label: chromatic button accordion
entries.gloss: Accordion with buttons arranged chromatically

entries.label: chuurqin
entries.gloss: Counter-trapezoid shaped Mongolian fiddle, it is the ancestor of the Morin khuur.

entries.label: cimbalom
entries.gloss: European hammered dulcimer

entries.label: cimbasso
entries.gloss: Its name variously used to describe the serpentone, the ophicleide and the bombardon, the modern cimbasso was developed by instrument making firm Pelitti under instruction guidance by Verdi; it had a forward facing bell and 3 to 6 valves. The modern instrument has a characteristic bend.

entries.label: cimpoi
entries.gloss: Known since the 15th century, it is made of a whole goat or sheep skin with fur either in or out. It has from 5 to 8 fingerholes and metalwork decorated wooden chanters.

entries.label: citole
entries.gloss: The citole is an archaic musical instrument, similar to and a distant ancestor of the modern guitar.

entries.label: cizhonghu
entries.gloss: The dahu, also known as cizhonghu or xiaodihu, is a large Chinese bowed string instrument in the huqin family.

entries.label: clapper
entries.gloss: Made of wood, bone or metal, this ancient instrument is the forerunner to many other struck idiophones.

entries.label: clapstick
entries.gloss: Used by Australian Aboriginals to maintain rhythm in chants and traditionally to accompany didgeridoo. There are also Boomerang clapsticks.

entries.label: classical guitar
entries.gloss: Also known as Spanish guitar, it is used in classical, folk and other styles, the strings are nylon or gut.

entries.label: classical kemençe
entries.gloss: Turkish bowl-shaped kemenche, mainly used in classical Ottoman music.

entries.label: clavinet
entries.gloss: Originally produced by Hohner from 1964 to 1982, it had keys with rubber-clad metal tines that tapped metal strings and two electric pickups. Its sound has been recreated in many modern synths.

entries.label: claviola
entries.gloss: Free reed melodica-like instrument that is worn like an accordion, with differing length pipes which control the pitch.

entries.label: clavioline
entries.gloss: An early analogue synthesizer, it had a vacuum tube oscillator and high/low pass filtering to produce vibrato.

entries.label: claviorganum
entries.gloss: Popular in the fifteenth century, it was a combination of a pipe organ and harpsichord, often with two keyboards, one for the strings and one for the pipes mounted underneath.

entries.label: cobla
entries.gloss: Generally used to accompany the traditional Catalan circle folk dance the sardana.

entries.label: cobla de tres quartans
entries.gloss: Precursor of the cobla used in sardana, it was in use since the medieval period.

entries.label: concert flute
entries.gloss: Western concert flute is the most common variant of the flute and is commonly referred to as just "flute".

entries.label: conch
entries.gloss: conch shell

entries.label: concussion idiophone
entries.gloss: Generally consists of two completely equal or somewhat unsymmetrical sticks, plates, shells or similar hit together.

entries.label: contrabass saxophone
entries.gloss: The largest and lowest pitch member of the saxophone family (ignoring the subcontrabass tubax).

entries.label: cor anglais
entries.gloss: While also known as English horn, it is neither a horn nor English, but a transposing member of the oboe family, pitched at F.

entries.label: cornamuse
entries.gloss:
For the French bagpipe, see cornemuse du centre.
For Italian cornamusa, see bagpipe.
Related to the crumhorn, it was used in the Renaissance. Because only a paragraph by Praetorius is the only known information, all reconstructions are approximations.

entries.label: cornemuse du Centre
entries.gloss:
Not to be confused with the Renaissance double-reed cornamuse.
For Italian cornamusa, see bagpipe.
While also a general term for bagpipes in French, they have two telescoping drones with single reeds and a double-reed chanter.

entries.label: cornet
entries.gloss: Early 19th century brass instrument with a conical bore, it is more compact and mellower than the trumpet which it resembles.

entries.label: cornett
entries.gloss:
Popular from 1500 to 1650, also known as zink, it was octagonal with seven holes like flute but mouthpiece like trumpet.
For the modern brass instrument, see cornet.

entries.label: cowbell
entries.gloss: Metal bell used in various genres, it is often attached to a drum kit.

entries.label: craviola
entries.gloss: Distinctly asymmetric in contrast to typical guitar, its timbre is a combination of the harpsichord (pt:cravo) and the Viola caipira. It can have six or twelve nylon or steel strings and are produced solely by company Giannini.

entries.label: crumhorn
entries.gloss:
Not to be confused with the 17-18 century French court oboe cromorne.
Used during the Renaissance, its double-reed is inside a windcap and its body ends in a decorative curve.

entries.label: cuatro
entries.gloss: A class of South-American guitars.

entries.label: cuíca
entries.gloss: Originating in Africa, it is used in carnivals and samba music. Consisting of a wooden or metal barrel, its single membrane has a tuning-stick attached.

entries.label: cylindrical drum
entries.gloss: A cylindrical drum is a straight-sided and generally two-headed drum.

entries.label: cymbal
entries.gloss: Various types of cymbal. Also called chũm chọe.

entries.label: cò ke
entries.gloss: The cò ke is an instrument used by the Mường ethnic minority in Vietnam. It is similar to the đàn nhị, consisting of a cylindrical wooden soundbox covered in snakeskin and two strings which are played with a horsehair bow.

entries.label: cümbüş
entries.gloss: Created by Zeynel Abidin Cümbüş, who named himself after it, it’s a banjolin-like modern Turkish instrument.

entries.label: daegeum
entries.gloss: The daegeum is a large transverse flute from Korea which is made of bamboo.

entries.label: daf
entries.gloss: The daf is a large Persian frame drum used in popular and classical music. The frame is usually made of hardwood with many metal ringlets attached and the membrane is usually goatskin.

entries.label: daire
entries.gloss: A larger version of tef, used to indicate the rhythmic structures (usul) in makam music.

entries.label: daluo
entries.gloss: The daluo is a Chinese large flat gong whose pitch drops when struck with a padded mallet.

entries.label: danso
entries.gloss: Used in folk music and educationally in Korean schools, it is a notched, vertically end-blown bamboo flute which, like its bigger cousin the Tungso, was derived from the Chinese xiao in the 19th century.

entries.label: daruan
entries.gloss: Bass member of Chinese ruan family of lutes.

entries.label: davul
entries.gloss: Davul, turkish drum

entries.label: dhol
entries.gloss: Double headed drum from India.

entries.label: dholak
entries.gloss: Classical North Indian hand drum.

entries.label: diatonic button accordion
entries.gloss:
For the organ also known as Melodeon, see reed organ.
For the mouth blown keyed MELODION, see melodica.
Also known as Melodeon, it has 1 to 2 rows of buttons that each produce two tones (bisonoric).

entries.label: diddley bow
entries.gloss: The diddley bow is a single-stringed American instrument which is typically homemade. It consists of a single string of baling wire tensioned between two nails on a board over a glass bottle, which is used both as a bridge and as a means to magnify the instrument's sound.

entries.label: dilruba
entries.gloss: The dilruba is a bowed string instrument from Northern India, mostly used in religious music and light classical songs.

entries.label: ding tac ta
entries.gloss: The ding tac ta is a free reed wind instrument played by the Ê Đê minority in Vietnam. It is made of a bamboo tube with three holes and a gourd wind chamber.

entries.label: disk drive
entries.gloss: Computer drives used for producing music, be it hard drives, floppy, CD or other.

entries.label: diyingehu
entries.gloss: The diyingehu is a Chinese bowed string instrument, with four strings and tuned like the double bass.

entries.label: dizi
entries.gloss: The dizi is a Chinese transverse flute typically made of bamboo. In Chinese, it is sometimes just called 笛 (di), but in Japanese 笛 (fue) is a more generic word referring to a whole class of flutes rather than this specific instrument.

entries.label: djoza
entries.gloss: Its origins can be sourced almost 5000 years ago, this Iraqi string instrument is the forefather of several instruments around the world. Its name means coconut or acorn, while originally made of walnut, it is today of coconut and fish-skin or heart-membrane.

entries.label: dohol
entries.gloss: The dohol is a large cylindrical drum used in Iran and Afghanistan.

entries.label: dolceola
entries.gloss: A dolceola is a musical instrument resembling a miniature piano, but which is in fact a zither with a keyboard.

entries.label: dombra
entries.gloss: The dombra is a long-necked lute from central Asia.

entries.label: domra
entries.gloss: The domra is a long-necked Russian string instrument of the lute family with a round body and three or four metal strings.

entries.label: donso ngɔni
entries.gloss: Six-stringed lute-harp from Wassoulou, West Africa. Traditionally played by hunters, its resonator box is made of calabash covered by animal skin.

entries.label: doshpuluur
entries.gloss: The doshpuluur is a long-necked Tuvan lute.

entries.label: double bass
entries.gloss: Known also as contrabass or upright bass, it is the largest and lowest-pitched member of the modern violin family and a principal member of the symphony orchestra.

entries.label: dramyin
entries.gloss: The dramyin is a traditional Himalayan long-necked lute with seven strings.

entries.label: drum machine
entries.gloss: drum programming

entries.label: drums (drum set)
entries.gloss: Set of drums developed from the 1930's onward, it is used in Jazz, Swing, Rock and Pop music. It consists of snare drum, tom-toms, hi-hats, cymbals and bass drum.

entries.label: duck call
entries.gloss: Short wooden flute used to imitate the sound of ducks.

entries.label: duduk
entries.gloss: The duduk is a traditional Armenian double reed woodwind instrument.

entries.label: dudy podhalanskie
entries.gloss: Known since the 16th century, it has 3 drones; one in a separate drone pipe and two in the chanter (which as three channels), it has no bells and is mouthblown.

entries.label: dudy wielkopolskie
entries.gloss: Originally played together with the special fiddle mazanki, today with prepared violin or solo, it has a single chanter with seven finger holes and a drone pipe folded back on itself twice both ending in curved bells.

entries.label: duggi
entries.gloss: Made of clay with two layers of goat skin, it is used as a rhythmic accompaniment to shehnai players and is one of the instruments of the Baul community.

entries.label: dulce melos
entries.gloss: European mediaeval struck string instrument, similar to the psaltery and a possible ancestor of the piano. Basically it is a dulcimer with keys.

entries.label: dulcian
entries.gloss:
Not to be confused with the Spanish double-reed dulzaina.
Used in the renaissance, it is made of maple wood with a folded bore and conical bell.

entries.label: dulcitone
entries.gloss: Like a piano, but here keyed hammers hit tuning forks.

entries.label: dulzaina
entries.gloss:
Not to be confused by the European renaissance bassoon dulcian.
Not to be confused with several Spanish bagpipes also called "gaita".
Widely used in Spanish communities it has many different names and a conical shape.

entries.label: dunun
entries.gloss: Dunun is a family of West African cylindrical drums.

entries.label: dutar
entries.gloss: The dutar is a long-necked two-stringed lute found in Iran and Central Asia.

entries.label: duxianqin
entries.gloss: The duxianqin is a one-string zither which is likely derived from the Vietnamese đàn bầu.

entries.label: dūdmaišis
entries.gloss: It has a single chanter and drone with a bag made of a variety of animals, it has fur out and an ornamental goats head. Traditionally played at spring festivities, recently it has had a resurgence.

entries.label: effects
entries.gloss: Effects refers to devices which enable a musician to modify the sound of an instrument.

entries.label: electric bass guitar
entries.gloss: Solid body 4-stringed electric bass guitar. The most common for "bass guitar" and "bass" credits in popular (rock) music.

entries.label: electric fretless guitar
entries.gloss: Electric guitar without frets.

entries.label: electric sitar
entries.gloss: Electric guitar with standard fretboard and tuning but added sympathetic strings and specialised bridge so the sound will resemble sitar, it became popular in rock, jazz and fusion music after its invention in the 1960's.

entries.label: electronic shruti box
entries.gloss:
Not to be confused with the analogue bellow powered shruti box or the string instrument tanpura.
Electronic synthesizer invented by Mr. G. Raj Narayan in 1979. By the 1990 models were using recording samples.

entries.label: elektronium
entries.gloss: In the form of a piano accordion, the keys control the output, pitch and sound, bellows control only volume. Sold by Hohner since 1952, it has gone through many modernisations through the years.

entries.label: erhu
entries.gloss: The erhu is a bowed Chinese instrument with two strings.

entries.label: esraj
entries.gloss: The esraj is a bowed string instrument from Eastern and Central India, mostly used as an accompanying instrument.

entries.label: fiddle
entries.gloss: Generally any bowed handle lute with the characteristic "violin" shape belong to fiddles.

entries.label: fife
entries.gloss: Small, high-pitched, transverse flute, similar to the piccolo, but with a narrower bore.

entries.label: fipple flute
entries.gloss: Fipple or duct flutes have a mouthpiece that is breathed into, but no reeds.

entries.label: fiscorn
entries.gloss:
For the instrument known in Italy as flicorno see saxhorn.
For the instrument known in Spain as fliscorno see flugelhorn.

Originating in Germanic polka bands, it is used today in Catalan cobla.

entries.label: five-string banjo
entries.gloss: The most common and based on the original design, its fifth string is shorter than the others, creating an uneven pitch progression.

entries.label: flageolet
entries.gloss: While today it is obscure, it was developed and improved for 400 years. The French flageolet has four holes in the front and two thumb holes in the back.

entries.label: flamenco guitar
entries.gloss: Deriving from the classical guitar, it has many modifications and playing techniques to create a more percussive sound. Originally having wooden tuning pegs like lutes and violins, it has a thinner, lighter build with "golpeadores" or tapping-plates and less sustain than the classical guitar.

entries.label: floppy disk drive
entries.gloss: Floppy drives configured to produce tones while reading, using software.

entries.label: flumpet
entries.gloss: As long as a trumpet, it shares the piston valve design of both instruments with a mellow sound between the two.

entries.label: flute
entries.gloss: Reedless aerophone, usually a tube.

entries.label: flutina
entries.gloss: Early predecessor to the diatonic accordion, it was similar to the German concertina and had 4 fold bellows and brass reeds.

entries.label: flûte d'amour
entries.gloss: The flûte d'amour is the mezzo-soprano instrument of the flute family.

entries.label: foot stomps
entries.gloss: Percussion performed with feet, such as foot tapping and clogging.

entries.label: footbass
entries.gloss: Large square spring-containing bellows operated by the feet, it was used by accordion players as bass accompaniment in early 20th century Wallonia.

entries.label: four-string banjo
entries.gloss: Lacking the short drone string of its predecessor, it is usually played with a plectrum and has 22 frets.

entries.label: fretless bass
entries.gloss: Variety of bass guitars without frets.

entries.label: friction idiophone
entries.gloss: Friction idiophones are idiophones where the sound is created by the instrument being rubbed.

entries.label: frottoir
entries.gloss: Dispenses with the frame altogether, and is worn as a vest, it is played with spoons or bottle openers.

entries.label: fujara
entries.gloss: The fujara is a large folk shepherd's fipple flute originated from central Slovakia.

entries.label: fundeh
entries.gloss: Middle size/pitch drum, it has a slack goat skin membrane and it is hit with the palms. Important in the Jamaican Burru music and Rastafari movement, it is part of the Nyabinghi/Akete drums.

entries.label: gaida
entries.gloss: Small Bulgarian/Macedonian and Balkan goat or sheep-skin bagpipe used in folk, pastoral or other traditional settings. There are many similarly named small bagpipes in this area.

entries.label: gaita asturiana
entries.gloss: Larger than the gallega, it has been in use since atleast the 13th century, traditionally with only one chanter and drone, it has very colourfully decorated fur.

entries.label: gaita de boto
entries.gloss: Historically solo instrument used in traditional and ritual dances, the drones have reinforced pewter rings and the goatskin bag is covered with a colourful fabric.

entries.label: gaita gallega
entries.gloss: Used at-least since the 9th century, it has two to three drones with bag and pipe both decorated with fur. Used in festivals by marching players accompanied by percussion.

entries.label: gaita sanabresa
entries.gloss: From Sanabria, it is distinct from other Spanish bagpipes, with its single drone and open fingering, it is accompanied by percussion in folk music.

entries.label: gajdy
entries.gloss: Czech-Polish bellow-blown large goatskin bag with a six finger hole chanter and a long angular drone pipe that is balanced over the shoulder, the two flared pipes have inlaid metal designs and can have goat head decorations.

entries.label: gambang
entries.gloss: Consists of up to 21 hardwood bars suspended by pins and rope over an oft ornate wooden trapeze shaped box, the two springy beaters are made of buffalo horn.

entries.label: game console sound chip
entries.gloss: Sound chip from various video game consoles, computers and similar, used for music, chiefly in bitunes and chiptunes.

entries.label: gamelan
entries.gloss:
Gamelan is basically split up in 3 traditions: the Balinese, the Sundanese and the Javanese, with each area having several different gamelan ensembles from large to small, each including a variety of instruments.
Most if not all gamelan instruments come in two scales, Sléndro and Pélog, these are tuned differently and large gamelan orchestras always include at-least one of each scale and often several sets in each.
Gamelan is an integrated part of Indonesian culture, is used in important traditions and throughout Indonesian life.

entries.label: gankogui
entries.gloss: Used as a rhythm keeper in large percussion orchestras by sub-saharan Ewe and Fon people, it is made of a sheet of metal forged and hammered into twin bells, hit with a wooden beater.

entries.label: ganzá
entries.gloss: Used in various performances (capoeira angola, caboclo, etc) and samba music, it is usually made of metal and filled with grains, pebbles or the like.

entries.label: gaohu
entries.gloss: The gaohu is a Chinese bowed string instrument developed from the erhu and tuned a fourth higher.

entries.label: garifuna drum
entries.gloss: Important to the Garifuna culture, it consists of two drums, the tenor, primero and the bass, segunda, each is made of hollowed out wood with membranes of pig, sheep or deer.

entries.label: garmon
entries.gloss: Used in Russian, Mari and Caucasus folk music, it has two rows of buttons in a diatonic scale, as well as additional bass buttons.

entries.label: gayageum
entries.gloss: The gayageum is a traditional Korean zither-like string instrument which normally has 12 strings.

entries.label: gehu
entries.gloss: The gehu is a Chinese bowed string instrument, with four strings and tuned like the cello.

entries.label: gemshorn
entries.gloss: Medieval or possibly older, it was historically made of goat-horns or, less commonly, clay. With only a few holes and a single octave range it was used pastorally. Modern revival variants are more complicated and are usually made of cattle-horn.

entries.label: gendèr
entries.gloss: Uses in Javanese gamelan and Balinese wayang, these range from 12 to 14 tuned bronze keys, all suspended over metal or bamboo resonators.

entries.label: gendèr barung
entries.gloss: Used for elaborate and complex parts, it has thinner but wider metal bars suspended above resonator rods, it is the middle-pitched member of the gendèr family.

entries.label: gendèr panerus
entries.gloss: Used for simple ornamentation, it has thick small metal bars suspended above resonator rods, it is the highest pitched member of the gendèr family.

entries.label: gendèr wayang
entries.gloss: Special version of the gendèr used in Gamelan gendèr wayang performances. Tuned in Slendro, one to two pairs are played using the same hand to both play and dampen the keys.

entries.label: geomungo
entries.gloss: The geomungo is a traditional Korean zither, based on the Chinese guqin, which typically has 6 strings.

entries.label: ghatam
entries.gloss: South Indian Carnatic percussion

entries.label: ghaychak
entries.gloss:
Having 4 metal strings, it is carved from a single piece of wood into a particular shape similar to the Sarinda, it has 3 soundholes, two on each side of the short neck and one under the bridge which is membrane-covered.
Not to be confused with the Uyghur spike fiddle ghijak.

entries.label: ghijak
entries.gloss: Not to be confused with the Persian lute ghaychak.

entries.label: gittern
entries.gloss: Round-backed lute ancestral to the guitar.

entries.label: gizmo
entries.gloss: An effects device to be clamped on the bridge, it produces “synthesizer-like” sounds.

entries.label: glass harmonica
entries.gloss: Taking the concept of musical glasses but mounting the incrementing bowls on a turnable spindle, it is played with damp fingers.

entries.label: glass harp
entries.gloss: Known in Persia as far back as the 14th century, it consists of glass containers, tuned by either being filled with water or later being of different sizes. Played by rubbing dampened fingers on the rims.

entries.label: glockenspiel
entries.gloss:
Common and popular metallophone, usually an arrangement of metal keys or slabs on a wooden resonator box.
For the instrument often used in bell towers, see carillon.
For the instrument called orchestra bell/chime in some languages, see tubular bells.

entries.label: goblet drum
entries.gloss: Goblet drums are single-headed drums with a goblet shaped body.

entries.label: gong
entries.gloss: Tuned metal discs

entries.label: gong bass drum
entries.gloss: A gong bass drum is a large single drumhead which resembles a gong.

entries.label: gong-chime
entries.gloss: Chiefly used in Southeast Asian music, these consist of from only 1 to several dozens of metal (often bronze) "kettles", set in a wide variety of different supports and played with mallets.

entries.label: gopichant
entries.gloss:
For the one stringed lute also called ektar/ektara, see tumbi.
For the similar looking instrument with only one spoke, see tun tuna.
Not to be confused with the ekatantri veena, an ancient Indian monochord.
It has a small, round or trapeze shaped body of wood or coconut with a membrane at the bottom. Attached to the sides is a neck of split bamboo from which a single string is suspended and attached to the membrane.

entries.label: gralla
entries.gloss: Dulzaina specifically from Catalonia.

entries.label: guban
entries.gloss: Important in Yue, Kunkqu and Peking opera, it consists of the drum bangu and the clapper paiban. Drum is played by one hand and clapper with the other.

entries.label: guitalele
entries.gloss: The guitalele is a guitar-ukulele hybrid, combining the small size of a guitalele with the six strings of a classical guitar.

entries.label: guitar family
entries.gloss: Please help move wrongly credited relationships from this, most if not almost all should probably just be "guitar" with credit (guitars).

entries.label: guitar synthesizer
entries.gloss: A guitar synthesizer is any one of a number of systems that allow a guitar player to play synthesizer sound.

entries.label: guitarrón chileno
entries.gloss: The guitarrón chileno is a Chilean guitar-like plucked string instrument which typically has 25 strings.

entries.label: guitarrón mexicano
entries.gloss: The guitarrón mexicano is a very large and deep-bodied Mexican guitar-like instrument with six strings which is traditionally played in mariachi groups.

entries.label: guitorgan
entries.gloss: Invented in 1966 by vox, and in 1969 by Bob Murrell, it is an electric guitar with electronic organ wiring and knobs added.

entries.label: gumbri
entries.gloss: Lute played by Gnawa people, its camel hide covered wooden soundbox has 3 goat gut strings.

entries.label: guqin
entries.gloss: The guqin is a plucked seven-string Chinese musical instrument of the zither family.

entries.label: gusli
entries.gloss: Ancient Russian psaltery/box-zither with 4 to 36 metal strings, it is played in a few different ways, depending on the variation (see annotation). Originally similar to a flat harp, it was played at ceremonies and other festivities.

entries.label: guzheng
entries.gloss: The guzheng or zheng is a Chinese plucked zither, with 18 to 23 or more strings and movable bridges.

entries.label: güira
entries.gloss: Made of metal with many small notches scraped with a brush or hair pick, it is used in merengue típico.

entries.label: güiro
entries.gloss: Made of gourd or wood, it is used as a scraper in Latin American music.

entries.label: haegeum
entries.gloss: Widely used in Korea, it has a wood soundbox and a rod neck with two silk-strings, heldt on the knee while played with a bow.

entries.label: handbell
entries.gloss: Open in one end, it has a strap to hold while ringing.

entries.label: handpan
entries.gloss: Invented initially as the Hang, it is made of two tuned metal convex pans glued together creating an UFO shape.

entries.label: hard disk drive
entries.gloss: Hard disk configured to produce tones in pattern.

entries.label: hardingfele
entries.gloss: Folk-fiddle from Hardanger, Norway. It has 4 melody- and 4-5 drone-strings, it is richly decorated and used in the traditional "halling" folk music and dance.

entries.label: harmonica
entries.gloss: Used especially in blues, American folk and country, it consists of a rectangle shape with soundholes along the wide side, where air is blown and drawn across free reeds which are mounted on a plate inside.

entries.label: harmonium
entries.gloss:
Not to be confused with European upright reed organ also commonly known as "Harmonium".
Also known as the samvadini, it was developed in India from imported reed organs. Consists of a wooden box-shape with a keyboard and a bellows in the back; both are operated by the same player, often a singer. While upright versions exist, they are rare.

entries.label: harp
entries.gloss: The harp is a plucked string instrument consisting of multiple strings stretched across a vertical frame.

entries.label: harp guitar
entries.gloss: The harp guitar is a guitar-based string instrument with any number of additional unstopped strings which can accommodate individual plucking.

entries.label: harpejji
entries.gloss: Effectively a small electric guitar-piano hybrid, it is played by tapping the multiple isometric arranged strings that are stretched over a long flat board.

entries.label: hi-hat
entries.gloss: A hi-hat is a typical part of a drum kit, consisting of a pair of cymbals mounted on a stand.

entries.label: hichiriki
entries.gloss: Used in gagaku, it is a double reed flute.

entries.label: hmông flute
entries.gloss: Family of Hmông flutes.

entries.label: hotchiku
entries.gloss: The hotchiku is a Japanese end-blown bamboo flute.

entries.label: hue puruhau
entries.gloss: Large gourd (hue) with no finger-holes, it is blown like a jug and has a booming bass sound.

entries.label: hue puruwai
entries.gloss: Gourd (hue) shakers with seeds intact

entries.label: hulusi
entries.gloss: The hulusi is a Chinese free reed wind instrument which has three bamboo pipes which pass through a gourd.

entries.label: hummel
entries.gloss: Whole or half-pear shaped wooden body, it is partly fretted and has two string-courses; melody and drone. The name comes from Germanic words meaning bumblebee or buzzing.

entries.label: huqin
entries.gloss: Chinese family of bowed spike-fiddles, usually with 2, occasionally 3-4 strings, the bodies made of wood and covered with skin occasionally thin wood or made of coconut.

entries.label: hydraulophone
entries.gloss: Made of tubing with holes that may have everything from none to two reeds, water instead of air comes out of the holes. Sound is produced by covering the holes with fingers, altering the flow of water through the holes.

entries.label: hyoshigi
entries.gloss: Used in traditional kabuki and bunraku theatre, it consists of two hardwood pieces tied together with ornamental cord.

entries.label: härjedalspipa
entries.gloss: Six holed fipple flute used traditionally in pastoral settings like its cousin the spilåpipa.

entries.label: hümmelchen
entries.gloss: Having a small bag, it has a soft sound. Its chanter and two drones of differing length are made of fruitwood. It historically had single reeds, modern creations are more complex and double-reeded.

entries.label: idiophone
entries.gloss: Without strings or membranes, sound is created by the whole instrument vibrating.

entries.label: igil
entries.gloss: The igil is a Tuvan bowed string instrument with two strings.

entries.label: janggu
entries.gloss: The janggu or janggo is a double-headed hourglass shaped drum which is the most widely used drum used in the traditional music of Korea.

entries.label: jantar
entries.gloss:
Stick zither from Rajasthan. It is made of wood with at least two large gourd resonators, the strings rest on very high frets.

Not to be confused with the 13th century tritantri-vina which evolved into the bin via a five-string stick-zither also known as "jantar".

entries.label: jegogan
entries.gloss: Largest and lowest pitched of the gangsa, it has 5 to 7 large metal bars suspended over long bamboo resonators.

entries.label: jeli ngɔni
entries.gloss: Four-stringed banjo-like lute from West Africa, traditionally played by griots. Made of hollowed out wood with an animal hide as membrane.

entries.label: jing
entries.gloss: The jing is a large gong used in traditional Korean music.

entries.label: jing'erhu
entries.gloss: The jing'erhu is a Chinese bowed string instrument, similar to the erhu, so named because is played in Beijing opera.

entries.label: jinghu
entries.gloss: The jinghu is a Chinese bowed string instrument with two strings used primarily in Beijing opera.

entries.label: jouhikko
entries.gloss: The jouhikko is a traditional, 2 or 3 stringed bowed lyre, from Finland and Karelia.

entries.label: jublag
entries.gloss:
Second lowest pitched of the gangsa, it has 4 to 7 bronze keys suspended over long bamboo resonators.
For the Sundanese bamboo xylophone also used in gamelan, see calung.

entries.label: jug
entries.gloss: An empty jug (usually made of glass or stoneware) played with the mouth.

entries.label: junjung
entries.gloss: Sacred cylindrical goat or cattle rawhide drum, traditionally it was held with straps or placed on a stand and played horizontally while walking to battle, on special state occasions and religious ceremonies.

entries.label: k'lông pút
entries.gloss: Played by manipulating the airstream through bamboo pipes using cupping and clapping, this Vietnamesian "Air Xylophone" was traditionally played in the rice-field.

entries.label: kacapi
entries.gloss: There are two kinds, boat shaped "mother" and "child" ones, originally made of a single piece of wood and descended from the kacapi pantun as used in epic story. And a flat box-zither made of wood used from the 1950's and in experimental music.

entries.label: kacapi indung
entries.gloss: Known as indung "mother" or parahu "boat", it has 18 brass strings each with its own pyramid shaped bridge. Shaped like a boat, its sound hole is at the bottom.

entries.label: kacapi rincik
entries.gloss: Known as rincik "child" it has 15 steel strings, it has individual bridges and a sound-hole in the bottom.

entries.label: kacapi siter
entries.gloss: Inspired by western zithers, it has 20 strings and is flatter than the other kacapis.

entries.label: kachva sitar
entries.gloss:
Flat-cut gourd sitar with 16 frets, 2 steel & 3 brass strings. In the 1820s it was used by Ghulam Mohammed to develop the surbahar.

Mistakenly re-named "Kachapi vina" in the 19th century by Tagore, that instrument was actually an ancient unrelated short-necked pear-shaped lute.

entries.label: kagurabue
entries.gloss: Used in gagaku, this traditional bamboo flute has six holes.

entries.label: kamale ngɔni
entries.gloss: Modern derivative of the donso ngɔni, it comes with more strings and is made of calabash. It became an important instrument in the rise of the Wassoulou music in the 80's and 90's.

entries.label: kamancheh
entries.gloss: Persian spike-fiddle

entries.label: kanjira
entries.gloss: South Indian frame drum

entries.label: kanklės
entries.gloss: Oldest instrument of Lithuania, it is made of a special tree in a trapezoid shape, it has a metalbar and wooden pegs at each side were 5 to 12 strings are strung.

entries.label: kannel
entries.gloss: National symbol of Estonia, related to Finnish kantele. While traditionally a small instrument with 5 to 7 strings, some newer versions are much bigger, with up to 50 strings.

entries.label: kantele
entries.gloss: Traditional and mythological psaltery of Finland, it comes in two versions; the oldest, a one piece bridge-less psaltery with 5 to 20 originally horsehair, later metal, strings and a modern "Concert" box-zither variant with a switch mechanism to alter the up to 40 strings sharps and flats.

entries.label: kantilan
entries.gloss: Highest pitched gangsa, it has 10 brass or bronze keys suspended over short resonating bamboo pipes set in an heavily ornate case.

entries.label: kanun
entries.gloss: Kanun, Arabic plucked strings

entries.label: kartal
entries.gloss: The kartal is an Indian percussion instrument with jingles, played with the hands, mainly used in Kirtans, Bhajans and in Rajastani folk music.

entries.label: kaval
entries.gloss: The kaval is a chromatic end-blown flute from the Balkans and Anatolia.

entries.label: kecer
entries.gloss: Used in both gamelan and Wayang puppet theatre, it consists of two small cymbals sets; the bottom pair affixed in a highly decorated rancak rack, their lose counterparts attached together by string.

entries.label: kemanak
entries.gloss: Bent into a ladle or banana like shape, it is a pair of bronze slit-drums hit with tabuh beaters.

entries.label: kemenche
entries.gloss: Made of wood, its soundbox is oblong and its neck is short.

entries.label: kemençe of the Black Sea
entries.gloss: Turkish box-shaped kemenche, mainly used for folk music.

entries.label: kempli
entries.gloss: Singular bronze gong-chime kettle set on a decorated jackfruit-wood box stand. Used as time or tempo keeper, it is struck on the boss with panggul beater, which provides reference point in the pokok.

entries.label: kempul
entries.gloss: Set of 6 to 10 smaller hanging pitched bronze gongs with a protruding centre knob struck with tabuh beaters. Higher pitched than the gong ageng, it is often hung together with it.

entries.label: kempyang
entries.gloss: Always used with ketuk, it consists of two bronze kettle-gongs, pitched a note apart. Ached top bossed gongs are sat in the highly decorated rancak frame, beaten with tabuh beaters by the same person.

entries.label: kendang
entries.gloss:
Used in many Southeast Asian countries, the body is made of woods like jackfruit or coconut, the heads of buffalo- and goat-hide.
There are 2 main groups:
  • The Java/Sunda set of 3 to 4 curve sided drums with heads of different sizes.
  • The Bali set of two pairs of straight sided drums, both heads same size.

entries.label: kendang lanang
entries.gloss: The smaller and higher pitched of the Bali kendang, it is the follower "male" drum.

entries.label: kendang wadon
entries.gloss: The larger and deeper pitched of the Bali kendang, it is the leader "female" drum.

entries.label: kendhang batangan
entries.gloss:
Middle sized kendang, it is used in lively and complex rhythms.
In Sunda it is known as kendhang ciblon.

entries.label: kendhang gendhing
entries.gloss:
Largest or "ageng" of the kendang, it is still smaller than the bedug.
In Sunda it is known as kendhang gedé.

entries.label: kendhang indung
entries.gloss: Played in ensemble with kulanter, it is set at an angle and played with hands or sticks. It has the designation of "mother".

entries.label: kendhang ketipung
entries.gloss:
Smallest of the kendang, it is has a special two-instrument use with the gendhing.
In Sunda it is known as kendhang katipung.

entries.label: kendhang kulanter
entries.gloss: Always used together with the indung, dual child drums are divided into the katipung ("besar" or larger) and the kutiplak ("kecil" or smaller).

entries.label: kendhang wayangan
entries.gloss: Middle sized kendang, it was traditionally used for the wayang dance.

entries.label: kenong
entries.gloss: Related to bonang, it consists of 3 decorated rancak frames that each hold 2 large arched (jaler) bronze gong-chimes hit by heavy tabuh beater(s).

entries.label: kepyak
entries.gloss: Used in wayang puppetry, it is made of 1 to 4 iron (sometimes bronze) plates hung by strings, The puppeteer uses a small mallet set in the foot to hit the plate(s).

entries.label: kethuk
entries.gloss: Always used with kempyang, it consists of a single bronze kettle-gong, pitched deeper than kempyangs'. Flat top bossed gong is sat in a highly decorated rancak frame, beaten with tabuh beaters by the same person.

entries.label: keyboard
entries.gloss: electronic or digital keyboard

entries.label: keyed box zither
entries.gloss: Composite chordophone, box zither where some or all strings are operated by typewriter-keys or buttons (keyboard).

entries.label: keyed brass instruments
entries.gloss: These have holes along the body and sound production is similarly to woodwinds.

entries.label: keytar
entries.gloss: Made portable with a shoulder-strap like a guitar, this electric keyboard has sound controls on the neck.

entries.label: khamak
entries.gloss:
Not to be confused with the two pronged gopiyantra/gopichan, the similar concept tuntuna, the dotara-like tokari or the pulluvan kudam.
Used in folk music of the Bengal, Odisha and north-east India, the soundbox is a drum-like wooden cylinder with a membrane at one end held underneath an arm, attached to the membrane is a single string which is plucked with a pick. It is known by many names.

entries.label: khene
entries.gloss: Traditional instrument from Laos, it is also used in Thailand and even Vietnam. it consists of 14 bamboo pipes with a small hollowed hardwood soundbox.

entries.label: khim
entries.gloss: Hammered dulcimer of Thailand and Cambodia it was imported via China.

entries.label: khlui
entries.gloss: Ancient reedless fipple flute made of bamboo.

entries.label: khong wong
entries.gloss: The khong wong is a gong circle consisting of a number of gongs in a horizontal circular rattan frame. The player sits in the middle.

entries.label: khong wong lek
entries.gloss: The khong wong lek is a gong circle used in Thai classical music. It has 18 tuned bossed gongs and is smaller and higher in pitch than the khong wong yai.

entries.label: khong wong yai
entries.gloss: The khong wong yai is a gong circle used in the music of Thailand. It has 16 tuned bossed gongs and is larger and lower in pitch than the khong wong lek.

entries.label: khulsan khuur
entries.gloss: Used for folk songs, particularly by young girls.

entries.label: khèn Mèo
entries.gloss: The khèn Mèo is a mouth organ used by the Hmong people. It has bamboo pipes (typically six) which each have a free reed.

entries.label: ki pah
entries.gloss: Cow horns without fingerholes, with mouthpiece and free reed.

entries.label: kinnari vina
entries.gloss: Used since medieval times in Karnatakan folk music, it has 3 resonators made of calabash. It is similar to the ancient bin.

entries.label: kkwaenggwari
entries.gloss: The kkwaenggwari is a small flat brass gong, typically about 20cm in diameter, which is used primarily in the folk music of Korea.

entries.label: klong khaek
entries.gloss: The klong khaek is a double-headed barrel drum from Thailand. The heads are different sizes.

entries.label: klong song na
entries.gloss: The klong song na is a barrel drum from Thailand. It is played with the hands and is used in the piphat ensemble.

entries.label: klong that
entries.gloss: Klong that are large barrel drums from Thailand. They are played in a pair using wooden sticks and are used in the piphat ensemble.

entries.label: klong yao
entries.gloss: The klong yao is a goblet drum from Thailand which is usually decorated with a colourful skirt.

entries.label: kokle
entries.gloss: Originating from 13th century Latvia, it is made of wood and have today nine to eleven, up to thirty-three strings tuned diatonically. Played horizontally on lap or table by plucking while muting chosen strings. Became in the 70's and 80's an important part of the folklore movement.

entries.label: kokyu
entries.gloss: Although similar to and introduced at the same time as the shamisen, it is unique to japan. With ebony neck and coconut body its three (rarely four) strings are played upright with a horsetail bow.

entries.label: komuz
entries.gloss: Possibly dating back as far as 6000 BC, it is a national symbol of the Kyrgyz. Made of a single piece of apricot or juniper wood with 3 gut stings, it has derivations in much of eastern Europe.

entries.label: kortholt
entries.gloss: The kortholt is a woodwind instrument that was popular in the Renaissance period.

entries.label: koto
entries.gloss: The koto is a traditional Japanese string instrument with 13 strings that are strung over 13 movable bridges along the width of the instrument.

entries.label: kotsuzumi
entries.gloss: The kotsuzumi or simply tsuzumi is an hourglass-shaped Japanese drum with cords that can be squeezed or released to increase or decrease the tension of the heads.

entries.label: krakeb
entries.gloss: Used in Gnawa music, it consists of two large iron shapes with round bowls tied together.

entries.label: krap
entries.gloss: Made of various materials, clappers are struck together to keep rhythm and time for use in ceremonies and rituals and to accompany dancing and singing.

entries.label: krap khū
entries.gloss: Used in folk music, bamboo is split into a pair of 40 cm long sticks which are hit together.

entries.label: krap phuang
entries.gloss: Used in royal ceremonies, played by striking against the palm, it is made of several pieces of wood, ivory and sheets of brass between two larger pieces of wood tied together by a string at one end.

entries.label: krap sēphā
entries.gloss: Used in the chant, sēphā, a pair of squared bevelled rosewood sticks around 21 cm long and 3-4 cm thick.

entries.label: krar
entries.gloss: The krar is a five or six-stringed bowl-shaped lyre from Eritrea and Ethiopia.

entries.label: kudüm
entries.gloss: Turkish pair of small, hemispherical drums.

entries.label: kèn bầu
entries.gloss: Used in the traditional music of Vietnam, it is made of wood with a gourdshaped bell.

entries.label: kèn lá
entries.gloss: The kèn lá is an instrument used by the Hmong minority of Vietnam which consists of a leaf which is curled up and positioned in the mouth so it vibrates when it is blown.

entries.label: kös
entries.gloss: A Turkish drum used in the traditional Ottoman military bands.

entries.label: kōauau
entries.gloss: Cross-blown flute made of stone, bone or wood. It is 10 to 39 cm long, with usually 3 holes, but everything from none to 5 is known.

entries.label: kōauau ponga ihu
entries.gloss: Nose flute made of gourd with two holes. While it is tiny, it has a huge sound.

entries.label: lamellaphone
entries.gloss: Lamellophones are a family of musical instruments which have one or more long thin plates - "lamella" or "tongues" - which are fixed at one end and free at the other end. The free end is plucked, causing the plate to vibrate.

entries.label: laouto
entries.gloss: Differs from other lutes in that its string tension is greater thus sounding more like the oud. From ancient Greece, it was used as an accompaniment to Cretan lyra.

entries.label: lap harp
entries.gloss: Used to teach children how to play, it is a simplified zither shaped like a trapezoid.

entries.label: laser harp
entries.gloss: A laser harp is an electronic musical instrument consisting of several laser beams to be blocked, in analogy with the plucking of the strings of a harp, in order to produce sounds.

entries.label: lasso d'amore
entries.gloss: The lasso d'amore, whirly tube or corrugaphone is a corrugated plastic tube which is spun in a circle.

entries.label: launeddas
entries.gloss: The launeddas is a typical Sardinian woodwind instrument, consisting of three pipes.

entries.label: lavta
entries.gloss: The lavta is a plucked string instrument from Greece and Turkey.

entries.label: limbe
entries.gloss: The limbe is a Mongolian transverse flute.

entries.label: lira da braccio
entries.gloss:
For the wheel-bowed instrument also called "lira", see hurdy-gurdy.
For the harp-like instrument, see lyre.
For the bowed lute, see Cretan lyra.

entries.label: lirone
entries.gloss: Popular late 16th to early 17th, it is the bass member of the lira family with between 9 and 16 strings and a fretted neck.

entries.label: lithophone
entries.gloss: Arrangement of struck tuned stone bars.

entries.label: liuqin
entries.gloss: Traditionally made of willow, it has four strings and a small, pear-shaped body. Played with a pick, it has a higher pitch than the pipa.

entries.label: low whistle
entries.gloss: Larger and deeper than the tin whistle, it was developed by Overton and made of aluminium.

entries.label: lute
entries.gloss: This is the specific instrument, for other, "lute-like" instruments, see lute family.

entries.label: luthéal
entries.gloss: The luthéal is a kind of hybrid piano which extends the register possibilities of a standard piano, created by Georges Cloetens.

entries.label: lyra viol
entries.gloss: Small bass viol, specialised for intricate polyphonics, it had a flatter bridge than the other bass viols.

entries.label: madal
entries.gloss: Madal, hand drum originating from Nepal

entries.label: maddale
entries.gloss: Maddale is a double-headed drum from Karnataka, India. It is the primary rhythmic accompaniment in Yakshagana.

entries.label: mandocello
entries.gloss: The mandocello is a plucked string instrument of the mandolin family, the equivalent to the cello in the violin family.

entries.label: mandoguitar
entries.gloss:
Unison course tuned 12 stringed electric guitar body with mandolin neck, it is tuned an octave higher than a conventional guitar, thus having the tonal range of the mandolin.
Not to be confused with flat-backed mandolin which is also sold as "mando-guitar".

entries.label: mandolute
entries.gloss: A mandolute is a North African fretted string instrument which combines a traditional oud string format with five pairs of metal strings.

entries.label: mandora / gallichon
entries.gloss: Invented by European luthiers in the first half of the 18th century, it had 6 to 7 single or double courses of gut strings and a long neck with either sharp or shallow angled pegbox.

entries.label: marimba lumina
entries.gloss: MIDI controller with a marimba-layout inspired control deck.

entries.label: marímbula
entries.gloss: The marímbula is a plucked box musical instrument from the Caribbean.

entries.label: mashak
entries.gloss: Used in rural weddings, it has twin single reed pipes, one melody, one drone. It is becoming increasingly rare due to being displaced by Scottish Highland pipes.

entries.label: matstsyanka
entries.gloss:
Used since ancient times, it is a smaller half round shape with the chanter in one end and drones in the other, there are two related types; from northern Belarus and east-south Lithuania one drone one chanter both having bowed horns at the end.
Secondly; the macianka duda without horns has 3 drones in one hole instead of one.

entries.label: mbira
entries.gloss: The mbira or kalimba (also known by many other names) is an African thumb piano.

entries.label: mellophone
entries.gloss:
Not to be confused with melophone, a bellowed free reed shaped like a lute.
Originating in the 19th century horn-design boom, it is used mostly in outside concert and marching music.

entries.label: mellotron
entries.gloss: An electromechanical piano

entries.label: melodica
entries.gloss: Popular as a musical education tool, it is usually made of plastic with a keyboard, its free-reed mouthpiece can also have an optional air tube. It has many brand names.

entries.label: melophone
entries.gloss:
Not to be confused with mellophone, a brass valved instrument.
Wooden body shaped like a lute, it has a bellow operated by a handle at the bottom and buttons operating the reeds in the “neck”.

entries.label: membranophone
entries.gloss: Any kind of instrument with membranes, usually variously sized drums.

entries.label: metallophone
entries.gloss: Consisting of tuned metal bars, slates or keys struck with mallets and arranged (often on resonators of sonorous material) in various scales. Compare xylophone for the wooden bar equivalent.

entries.label: mezwed
entries.gloss:
Not to be confused with the Libyan shawm also known as zukra or zurna.
Not to be confused with mijwiz or the similar zummara.

Also do not confuse with "mizmar" a general Arabian term for several reed instruments, players of the same as well as a dance.

Used in traditional music together with drums, it has a small bag made of ewe or goat and double chanters with bells made of cowhorn.

entries.label: mijwiz
entries.gloss: Played using circular breathing, it is made of twin bamboo reeds with five to six holes. From the middle-east, it is used in traditional music and as a accompaniment to belly dancing and dabke.

entries.label: minipiano
