entries.gloss: The minipiano is a type of piano in which the sound producing mechanism is positioned below the keyboard, allowing an economical use of space.

entries.label: mirliton
entries.gloss: Simultaneously a woodwind and membranophone, sound is produced by singing or speaking into a thin buzzing membrane.

entries.label: monkey stick
entries.gloss: Homemade combination of a wooden pole with beer bottle tops and other jingles and a hefty boot at the bottom to create thumping bass, it is often decorated with hats, hair or stuffed animals.

entries.label: morin khuur
entries.gloss: Important to the Mongolians, it is trapezoid shaped with two traditionally horsehair, now often nylon, strings fastened by wooden pegs at the end which is carved like a horse head.

entries.label: morsing
entries.gloss: Indian mouth harp, played in Carnatic and Rajastani folk music.

entries.label: mouth harp
entries.gloss: Plucked by the mouth, it consists of a characteristically shaped frame with a metal or bamboo reed (tine). There are many variants around the world.

entries.label: mouth organ
entries.gloss: A mouth organ is a generic term for free reed aerophone with one or more air chambers fitted with a free reed.

entries.label: mridangam
entries.gloss: The mridangam is a double-sided drum from India.

entries.label: mukkuri
entries.gloss: Ingenious to the Ainu, it is made of bamboo with a string that vibrated creates sound.

entries.label: musette de cour
entries.gloss:
For the instrument known as "chinese musette", see suona.
For the oboe also known as musette, see piccolo oboe.
Also known as baroque musette, it was a small bagpipe used predominantly by French court and nobility in the 1600-1700's.

entries.label: musical saw
entries.gloss: Regular or specialised saw used for music, held and bent, it is bowed to produce characteristical glissando.

entries.label: nabal
entries.gloss: Used in traditional music, it's long and straight.

entries.label: nadaswaram
entries.gloss: Similar to the north Indian shahnai, it has a 95 cm long hardwood body with 7 finger holes and 5 wax-fillable tuning holes and a wide flaring wooden bell; shorter variants have a metal bell.

entries.label: nagadou-daiko
entries.gloss: The nagadou-daiko is an elongated barrel-shaped Japanese drum.

entries.label: nai
entries.gloss: Used traditionally since 16th-17th century by lǎutari, it is made of bamboo or reed stopped with cork and beeswax set in a curved bottom bar.

entries.label: naobo
entries.gloss: Chinese cymbals specially used in the Beijing opera.

entries.label: natural brass instruments
entries.gloss: Natural brass instruments only play notes in the instrument's harmonic series.

entries.label: natural horn
entries.gloss: Ancestor of the modern horn, it consists of a coiled tubing with a large flared bell. Bugles, posthorns and hunting horns are all natural horns.

entries.label: natural trumpet
entries.gloss: Ancestor of the modern trumpet, it is valveless with a mouthpiece and at-least one coil, it has an origin in military use.

entries.label: neyanban
entries.gloss: Often colourfully decorated, it is known since ancient times in southern Persia. It has a single reed with a double piped chanter with 6-7 holes.

entries.label: nguru
entries.gloss: Small vessel flute made of wood, clay, bone or soft stone like soapstone, it has 4 holes and is played with the nose or mouth.

entries.label: ngɔni
entries.gloss: A lute from West Africa, made of wood or gourd.

entries.label: njarka
entries.gloss: Made of goatskin covered dried gourd, it has a single gut string bowed with a horsehair bow.

entries.label: nohkan
entries.gloss: The nohkan is a high-pitched bamboo transverse flute from Japan.

entries.label: nose flute
entries.gloss: The nose flute is a flute played by the nose commonly found in countries in and around the Pacific.

entries.label: nose whistle
entries.gloss: The nose whistle (also known as the Humanatone) is a simple instrument played with the nose. The stream of air is directed over an edge in the instrument and the frequency of the notes produced is controlled by the volume of air.

entries.label: nyatiti
entries.gloss: The nyatiti is a five to eight-stringed plucked string instrument from Kenya.

entries.label: nyckelharpa
entries.gloss: The nyckelharpa is a traditional Swedish string instrument.

entries.label: oboe
entries.gloss: Oboe (soprano)

entries.label: oboe d'amore
entries.gloss: Oboe d'amore / Oboe d'amour (mezzo-soprano)

entries.label: oboe da caccia
entries.gloss: First referred to in 1722, this transposing double-reed has a curved tube and a flared (brass) bell.

entries.label: octave mandolin
entries.gloss: The octave mandolin is a fretted string instrument with four pairs of strings tuned in fifths, G, D, A, E (low to high), an octave below a mandolin.

entries.label: octavilla
entries.gloss: Used in Spanish classic and popular music during the late 19th and early 20th century, it together with bandurria and laúd carried the melody in rondas and rondallas. It had six pairs of strings, tuned a fourth lower than bandurria, It fell out of use when contralto bandurria became common.

entries.label: octavina
entries.gloss: Originating with the Spanish influence on Filipino culture, it has 14 strings and a short neck with 16 to 20 frets. It is played with its close relative, the laúd.

entries.label: octoban
entries.gloss: Small but long tom-toms set in groups of four or eight, they are a common addition in drumsets. Originally made of fibreglass, today also acrylic, aluminium or wood is used, and homemade ones of f.ex PVC are not uncommon.

entries.label: octobass
entries.gloss: Constructed as the uttermost largest member of the violin family, it is up towards 4 meters and has three strings operated by levers and pedals.

entries.label: oktawka
entries.gloss: Small Polish traditional fiddle.

entries.label: olifant
entries.gloss: Hunting horn carved out of ivory, it was widely used in Medieval wars to alarm or increase soldiers' morale.

entries.label: ondioline
entries.gloss: One of the first analogue synths, it had a filter bank with 15 sliders for different sounds, and a “vibrato” inducing keyboard based on the ondes Martenot’s.

entries.label: orpharion
entries.gloss: Invented in 16th century England, it had low-tension metal strings and sloping frets.

entries.label: orphica
entries.gloss: Portable piano with shoulder strap invented in 1795, it is a descendant of the Baroque Bauchladenspinett and a sort of early precursor of the keytar.

entries.label: other instruments
entries.gloss: Other instruments. If you can't find an instrument, please request it.

entries.label: oval spinet
entries.gloss: More accurately a virginals, its strings were arranged in a pattern creating an oval shape, allowing for a stronger, more compact configuration. 2 examples survive today.

entries.label: pahū
entries.gloss: Logs or thick planks up to 9 meters long used as signalling drums, as gongs for both war and peace. Even living hollowed trees have been used as pahū.

entries.label: pahū pounamu
entries.gloss: Gong made of pounamu; greenstone and pilot-whale bone with a striker made of akeake, a hardwood.

entries.label: paiban
entries.gloss: Made of sandalwood or bamboo, 2 blocks are tied together with a string, a third with a ribbon. Part of the drum and clapper ensemble guban, but confusingly, the clapper alone can also be called guban.

entries.label: pakhawaj
entries.gloss: Used in Hindustani dhrupad, this two-headed barrel-drum is tuned like its descendant the tabla.

entries.label: pan flute
entries.gloss: Named after the Greek god Pan, they are a selection of end-blown pipes made of reeds, bamboo, wood or similar. Many different variations exists around the world, especially in South America.

entries.label: pang gu ly hu hmông
entries.gloss: A “slide whistle”-like type of Hmông flute.

entries.label: pardessus de viole
entries.gloss: Pardessus or sopranino member of the viol family.

entries.label: parkapzuk
entries.gloss: Has a bag made of goat, veal or sheepskin, and a double piped chanter collected in a single horn. Both wooden chanters have holes; one for melody, the other for drone.

entries.label: pedal accordion
entries.gloss: Developed in Warszaw, Poland, it is used in folk music. It has two foot-operated bellows attached via metal/brass pipe; its body-bellows are only used for accents.

entries.label: pedal piano
entries.gloss: The pedal piano is a kind of piano that includes a pedalboard, enabling bass register notes to be played with the feet, as is standard on the organ.

entries.label: pemade
entries.gloss: Second highest pitched gangsa, it is deeper than the kantil but also has 10 brass or bronze keys suspended over short resonating pipes set in an heavily ornate case.

entries.label: percussion
entries.gloss: Very wide grouping, played by hitting directly aka idiophones and membranophones (from drums to xylophones). Use the closest approximate instrument possible for credits, use percussion with a credit if no better can be found and create an instrument ticket if necessary.

entries.label: percussion idiophone
entries.gloss: Generally consists of one to very many plates, sticks, or other objects hit with (or against) various types of mallets.

entries.label: pi
entries.gloss: Family of quadruple reed oboes.

entries.label: pi nai
entries.gloss: The pi nai is a type of pi normally used in the piphat ensemble.

entries.label: piano duo
entries.gloss: Chamber ensemble where two pianists play on a different piano each.

entries.label: piano four hands
entries.gloss: Chamber ensemble where two pianists play on the same piano at the same time.

entries.label: piano quartet
entries.gloss: ensemble of piano, violin, viola and cello

entries.label: piano spinet
entries.gloss: Small piano with drop action stickers manufactured from around 1930 to the early 1990s.

entries.label: piano trio
entries.gloss: Chamber ensemble of three players (one piano, one violin, one cello).

entries.label: piccolo oboe
entries.gloss: The piccolo oboe is the smallest and highest pitched member of the oboe family.

entries.label: piffero
entries.gloss:
For the small flute used with drum, see fife.
Often accompanied by accordions or bagpipes such as zampogna or müsa, it has 8-9 holes and a conical bore. In Sicily there was a larger bass version named bifora or pifara.

entries.label: pipa
entries.gloss: Chinese pear-shaped plucked lute with four strings and 12 to 26 frets.

entries.label: pipe and tabor
entries.gloss: Originally an early European combination of a drum (tambourine) and pipe (fipple flute) were pipe was played by one hand and drum beaten by the other. It was chiefly used for dancing music. It has analogies all over the world.

entries.label: piri
entries.gloss: The piri is a Korean double reed instrument made of bamboo, used in both the folk and classical (court) music of Korea. Related to the Chinese guan and Japanese hichiriki.

entries.label: piva
entries.gloss: Traditionally played with the piffero in folk ensambles, the bag is usually made of kid-leather with 2 drones: a bass and a tenor and a chanter with 7-8 finger-holes.

entries.label: pkhachich
entries.gloss: The pkhachich is a traditional shaken percussion instrument of the Circassian peoples.

entries.label: plucked idiophone
entries.gloss: Plucked idiophones have spikes, nails or flexible tongues ("lamellae") that are plucked in various ways to produce sound.

entries.label: pluriarc
entries.gloss: From West Africa, it has multiple curved necks each with one string, sometimes played a harp and sometimes with stops like a lute.

entries.label: poi
entries.gloss: Flax leaf balls filled with seeds, swung around to create rhythmic and visual patterns. An important element in the dance also known as poi.

entries.label: poi āwhiowhio
entries.gloss: A hollowed out gourd (hue) with one to three holes, swung around creating a whistling, chattering sound that resembled birds.

entries.label: porotiti
entries.gloss: Whirring, spinning disks of many shapes, sizes and materials. When blown on, they also create a well of different humming sounds.

entries.label: portative
entries.gloss: Constructed in medieval Europe to be as portable as possible, small upright wooden frame with keyboard contains a row of flute-pipes fed air from hand operated bellows.

entries.label: post horn
entries.gloss: Developed as early as the 1500-hundreds and used for mail-carrier signalling, it was coiled (usually just once) and valveless.

entries.label: practice chanter
entries.gloss: Looks like a recorder, but with double reeds and bagpipe fingering system. Mostly used to learn how to play the pipes, but are occasionally played in their own right.

entries.label: prepared piano
entries.gloss: A prepared piano is a piano that has had its sound altered by placing objects (preparations) between or on the strings or on the hammers or dampers.

entries.label: primero
entries.gloss: Tenor member of the garifuna drum group.

entries.label: pí thiu
entries.gloss: Pí thiu or Pí khui vertical flute

entries.label: pākuru
entries.gloss: Two rods, one is held in the mouth, which works as a resonance chamber while chanting and singing, the other is used for tapping and scraping, creating rhythm.

entries.label: pātē
entries.gloss: The pātē is a Polynesian slit drum made from a hollowed-out log.

entries.label: pōrutu
entries.gloss: A longer version of the kōauau, it is from 30-40 cm up towards 60 cm in length and often made of bone and hardwoods such as porokaiwhiria, mataī and tutu.

entries.label: pūkaea
entries.gloss: Up to 2,5 meters long, this wooden trumpet was used for a variety of announcements like war, welcoming people and kumara planting.

entries.label: pūmotomoto
entries.gloss: Long wooden flute with a notched open top and a single finger hole near the end.

entries.label: pūpakapaka
entries.gloss: A pūtātara with a long wooden mouth piece, it has a deeper timbre than the pūtātara.

entries.label: pūrerehua
entries.gloss: Made of wood, bone or stone, it has a long string attached. When spun around it produces a deep, loud whizzing sound that can be heard from far away.

entries.label: pūtātara
entries.gloss: Trumpet made of conch shell, it has a beautifully carved wooden mouthpiece. It was for signalling, but also ceremonial and ritual use.

entries.label: pūtōrino
entries.gloss: Made of wood and shaped after the casemoth cocoon, it can be played as both a flute (female voice) and a trumpet (male voice).

entries.label: qilaut
entries.gloss: The qilaut is an Inuit frame drum which has a handle and is made of caribou skin.

entries.label: quena
entries.gloss: Used in traditional Andean music, it is the smallest of its family

entries.label: quijada
entries.gloss: Made of an equine jawbone, it is used in traditional Latin American music as a rattle.

entries.label: rammana
entries.gloss: The rammana is a frame drum used in classical Thai and Cambodian music which forms one part of thon and rammana.

entries.label: ranat ek
entries.gloss: The ranat ek is a Thai xylophone which consists of 21 wooden bars suspended by cords over a boat-shaped trough resonator and struck by two mallets.

entries.label: ranat kaeo
entries.gloss: The ranat kaeo is a Thai instrument similar to a xylophone consisting of glass bars of varying lengths.

entries.label: ranat thum
entries.gloss: The ranat thum is a xylophone from Thailand consisting of 18 wooden bars suspended by cords over a boat-shaped trough resonator. It is similar to the ranat ek but lower in pitch.

entries.label: rauschpfeife
entries.gloss: Name also used in general for reed pipes from the 16th century, it has a conical bore and a windcap.

entries.label: ravanahatta
entries.gloss: Ancient bowed fiddle, once popular in Western India and Sri Lanka.

entries.label: rebab
entries.gloss:
"Rebab" (and other variant spellings) is the name for chiefly these 3 types of bowed/plucked string instrument families:
  • Large, short necked boatshaped "sarinda" type, here the kabuli rebab.
  • Small, long necked spike fiddle "huqyin" type, here the Indonesian rebab.
  • various sizes, varying necklength, pearshaped "Cretan lyra" type, here the bowed lutes proper.


Given the name cross-overs they are confused with eachother in most sources. Curiously, this cross-over confusion extends to related but separately or similarly named instruments as well, for example Ghijak (a spikefiddle) and Ghaychak (a boat-shaped).
It is, for the meantime, unknown how, if at all, these 3 subtypes are related.

For the spike fiddle used in gamelan, see Indonesian rebab.
For the plucked, boat-shaped Afghani instrument also know as kabuli rabab, see rubab.
For the medieval Indian plucked lute see Seni rebab.
For the medieval European pear-shaped fiddle see rebec.

entries.label: rebec
entries.gloss: With a pear shaped body made from a single piece of wood, this medieval bowed string instrument originated as a Byzantian lyra-like variant of the Arabic rebab and was a possible influence to the violin.

entries.label: reclam de xeremies
entries.gloss:
For the Mallorcan bagpipe, see xeremies.
For the Latin American oboe, see chirimía.
For the mediaeval woodwind, see shawm.
Made of two tied together cane tubes with a single-reed each, they each have 4 sound-holes in front, and traditionally, one in the back.

entries.label: reco-reco
entries.gloss: Originally made of bamboo or wood, it is now metal with springs and is used in Brazilian music.

entries.label: recorder
entries.gloss:
Family of end-blown woodwind flutes with a thumb-hole and seven finger-holes, it is the most common flute in Western classical tradition.
The family consists of a wide assortment of sizes:
  • garklein recorder
  • sopranino recorder
  • soprano recorder (descant)
  • alto recorder (treble)
  • tenor recorder
  • bass recorder
  • great bass recorder (c-bass)
  • contrabass recorder
  • subcontrabass recorder

Not to be confused with the transverse (side-blown) Western concert flute.

entries.label: reed organ
entries.gloss:
For the accordion also known as Melodeon, see diatonic button accordion.
For the mouth blown keyed MELODION, see melodica.
For the portable reed organ used in India see harmonium.
Also known as pump organ, it is large, looks like an upright piano and has pedals attached to bellows with reeds. Sound is produced by playing the keyboard.

entries.label: regal
entries.gloss: Popular in the renaissance, it was small and portable with two bellows and brass reeds.

entries.label: rehu
entries.gloss: Made of wood like mataī or tutu, this long flute has a transverse blowing hole with a fipple like European flutes but finger holes in the style of the traditional pōrutu.

entries.label: renaissance rackett
entries.gloss: Originating 1590 or earlier and made of wood or ivory, it had nine parallel cylindrical bores joined up at the top and bottom creating a continuous bore like a curled up snake. Its reed is attached to a center pirouette.

entries.label: repeater
entries.gloss: Also known as kette or keteh, it is the smallest size/pitch drum. It has a tight goat skin membrane and it is struck with the fingertips. Important in the Jamaican Burru music and Rastafari movement, it is part of the Nyabinghi/Akete drums.

entries.label: repinique
entries.gloss: The repinique is a cylindrical drum from Brazil.

entries.label: resonator guitar
entries.gloss: Dobro, resonator guitar

entries.label: reyong
entries.gloss: Set of 4 to 12 small metal gongs suspended in a string carriage, played by two to four players.

entries.label: riq
entries.gloss: The riq is a type of tambourine used as a traditional instrument in Arabic music.

entries.label: rondador
entries.gloss: Made of cane, it is used in Ecuador.

entries.label: ronroco
entries.gloss: An octave lower than the charango, it is the largest member of the family.

entries.label: ruan
entries.gloss: Family of Chinese plucked lutes.

entries.label: rubab
entries.gloss: Related to bowed instrument rebab, it is played in many countries, from India to Afghanistan. It's made of wood and covered with a membrane and has 3 melody strings, 3 drone strings and 11/12 resonance strings.

entries.label: rudra veena
entries.gloss: Considered the originator of all Indian strings (veena) it was used for ritual and meditation, North Indian raga and Dhrupad music. It has two dried gourd resonators and a body of bamboo with 24 wooden frets and 4 main, 2-3 secondary and one drone string.

entries.label: ryuteki
entries.gloss: Used in gagaku, it is a transverse flute.

entries.label: rōria
entries.gloss: Thin quiet mouth harp like instrument made of wood or bone.

entries.label: sabar
entries.gloss: The sabar is a drum from Senegal which is normally played with one hand and one stick. The body is an elongated cylinder with tapered ends. The head is made of goatskin and is attached to the body using pegs.

entries.label: sac de gemecs
entries.gloss: Very similar to the xeremies, the main difference being that here all the drones are functional.

entries.label: saduk
entries.gloss: A cross between a saxophone and a duduk invented and played by Alexander Berne.

entries.label: saluang
entries.gloss:
Used traditionally by the Minang people of West Sumatra for love songs, in shamanic rites and for capturing tigers, this open end-blown bamboo flute can be decorated to resemble tiger-stripes. Played with a circular breathing technique, it is 75 cm long with 3 to 6 holes depending on subtype.
  • saluang darek "inland" 4 holes
  • saluang pauh/padang 6 holes
  • saluang sungai pagu 3 holes

entries.label: samba whistle
entries.gloss: The samba whistle is a tri-tone whistle used in samba music and other Brazilian music styles.

entries.label: samica
entries.gloss: Also known as dangubica or kuterevka, it is similar to the bisernica and the ancestor of the entire tamburica ensemble. This plucked long-necked lute has two double strings and is played solo.

entries.label: sanshin
entries.gloss: The sanshin is an Okinawan string instrument which consists of a snakeskin-covered body, neck and three strings. It is traditionally played with a plectrum made of horn worn on the index finger.

entries.label: santoor
entries.gloss: Ancient hammered dulcimer with trapezoid walnut or maple soundbox, 25 bridges each with 4 strings that are hit by special mallets called mezrab. Used in traditional, folk and mystic Sufi music.

entries.label: sanxian
entries.gloss: The sanxian is a Chinese lute with three strings.

entries.label: sarangi
entries.gloss: The sarangi is a short-necked, bowed string instrument from India, Nepal and Pakistan.

entries.label: saron barung
entries.gloss: Often called simply "saron", it plays the basic, balungan melody.

entries.label: saron demung
entries.gloss: Called simply "demung", it is the largest and deepest pitched of the regular saron.

entries.label: saron family
entries.gloss:
Part of the Sundanese gamelan, these consist of a decorated wood resonator (rancak) upon which is resting six to nine thick, smooth, bronze or iron keys that are hit with mallets of hard wood or buffalo horn.

The saron family consists of the smallest member; saron panerus, the middle pitch member; saron barung and the largest member; sarong demung. Additionally, the largely obsolete slentho (which has been subsumed by the slenthem) is even deeper than the demung and the saron peking, which is a special slendro variant is even higher than the panerus, of which it shares an overlapping range. Finally the saron wayang is used in wayang performances.

entries.label: saron panerus
entries.gloss: Called simply "panerus", it has seven bronze keys resting on a decorated rancak box. Keys are hit by tabuh mallet with head of buffalo horn.

entries.label: saron peking
entries.gloss: Similar to panerus with which it has a different but overlapping range, it has 6 bronze keys tuned for the slendro key.

entries.label: saron wayang
entries.gloss: Used in the Javanese Wayang puppet theatre, it has nine large bronze keys set in a decorated frame.

entries.label: sarrusophone
entries.gloss: The sarrusophone is a family of transposing musical instruments, intended to serve as a replacement in wind bands for the oboe and bassoon.

entries.label: sasando
entries.gloss: Made of palmyra leaves that act as a resonator and a bamboo-tube stuck with wooden pegs where the plucked strings are attached, this traditional Indonesian instrument has an important place in folk history. It is still being used and modernised.

entries.label: satsuma biwa
entries.gloss: Supposedly created as a modification of the moso biwa as a boost for samurai, it has four strings and elevated frets, a large plectrum called Bachi is used.

entries.label: saw sam sai
entries.gloss: The saw sam sai is a three-stringed bowed instrument from Thailand.

entries.label: saw u
entries.gloss: The saw u is a Thai bowed string instrument which has a soundbox made from a coconut shell with a cowskin resonator.

entries.label: saxophone quartet
entries.gloss: Ensemble of four saxophones, generally SATBar.

entries.label: segunda
entries.gloss: Bass member of the garifuna drum group.

entries.label: seni rebab
entries.gloss: Larger, with a longer neck than the kabuli rabab, it has a hide covered soundbox and wooden fingerboard with mostly gut strings, it was developed during medieval times by Tansen, who improved it and gave it metal sympathetic strings.

entries.label: setar
entries.gloss: Derived from the Indian tritantri veena by the Persian poet Amir Khusro sometime in 13th century, it had 3 (now 4) strings and a long neck. It later gave name to the Indian sitar.

entries.label: shaken idiophone
entries.gloss: Shaken idiophone or rattle. Sound is produced by holding or containing usually small concussing parts.

entries.label: shakers
entries.gloss: Tube made of metal or bamboo, it is filled with seeds, pebbles or sand. Especially used in Latin American music, it is shaken rhythmically to produce sound.

entries.label: shakuhachi
entries.gloss: Japanese end-blown flute

entries.label: shawm
entries.gloss:
Not to be confused with zummara or other double clarinets with similar names.
For the multiple bore free reed created in 1880, see Martinshorn.
For the similarly named single-reed woodwind, see chalumeau.
For the Japanese descendant named from Portuguese, see charumera.
For the Catalan shawm, see tible.
For the Italian ciaramella, see piffero.
For the bagpipe, see xeremies.

European medieval and Renaissance conical bore double-reed woodwind, two types evolved; one from Middle-Eastern instruments and one from bagpipe chanters. A combination of both were used to develop the modern oboe.

entries.label: shehnai
entries.gloss: From the Indian subcontinent, it is used at marriages, in temples and concerts - made of wood with a double reed and wood/metal flared bell, it has 6-9 holes.

entries.label: shekere
entries.gloss: West African gourd-shaker, a net of beads covers it.

entries.label: sheng
entries.gloss: The sheng is a Chinese free reed instrument consisting of a number of vertical pipes.

entries.label: shichepshin
entries.gloss: The shichepshin is a traditional bowed string instrument of the Circassian peoples.

entries.label: shime-daiko
entries.gloss: The shime-daiko is a small Japanese drum with a short but wide body which has a higher pitch than a normal taiko.

entries.label: shinobue
entries.gloss: Japanese high-pitched transverse flute

entries.label: sho
entries.gloss: It is based on the Chinese sheng, but is smaller.

entries.label: shofar
entries.gloss: Ram's horn natural brass

entries.label: shruti box
entries.gloss: The shruti box is similar to a harmonium and is used to provide a drone accompaniment.

entries.label: shudraga
entries.gloss: The shudraga is a Mongolian fretless lute with three strings.

entries.label: siku
entries.gloss:
For the Italian bagpipe, see zampogna.
Also known as zampona, traditional Andean panpipe has two rows of pipes tied together with colourful bands.

entries.label: sistrum
entries.gloss:
Used in sacred rituals, it is made of metal or clay rattle with metal discs which jangle when shook.
Not to be confused with the West African calabash sistrum or disc rattle (n'goso m'bara).

entries.label: sitar
entries.gloss: Soundbox made of gourd, it has 18-21 (6-7 on frets and 11-15 sympathetic under the frets) metal strings, two bridges and a long wooden neck where the tuning pegs of the sympathetic strings are attached. Used in India since ancient times, it flourished during the 16-17th before arriving at it's current form in the 18th century. It became popular worldwide in the 1950-60.

entries.label: slapstick
entries.gloss: Often known as whip, it consists of two parts joined together by a hinge, it creates a whip-like sound when clacked together.

entries.label: slenthem
entries.gloss: Used in Javanese gamelan, the 6(slendro)-7(pelog) bronze keys beat by a disk mallet(tabuh) are suspended above individual tube metal/bamboo resonators set in a 75 cm long wooden frame.

entries.label: slentho
entries.gloss: Unlike the other saron, its six-seven keys are not smooth, but bevelled or bossed, like the gendèr and the slenthem, which has largely replaced it in the modernised gamelan.

entries.label: slide brass instruments
entries.gloss: Slide brass instruments use a slide to change the length of tubing.

entries.label: slide whistle
entries.gloss: Also known as swanee whistle or piston flute, it consists of a mouthpiece similar to the one of a recorder and a tube with a piston that varies the pitch. It is often used as a sound effect.

entries.label: slit drum
entries.gloss: Made of hollowed out wood or bamboo, it has incisions or slits as soundholes. Slit drums are among the most ancient and earliest instruments.

entries.label: somu dūdas
entries.gloss:
Used since the 16th century, it is made of lamb, kid or in the north, sealskin. it has1-2 drones and a chanter with 4-7 fingerholes.

The name dudy/duda(s) is used for very many folk bagpipes in Europe and western Asia - see annotation(s) for more.

entries.label: song loan
entries.gloss: The song loan is a traditional Vietnamese instrument consisting of a hollow wooden body (about 7 cm in diameter) attached to a flexible spring with a wooden ball on the other end and played with the foot.

entries.label: sopilka
entries.gloss: Sopilka (generally) refers to a type of fife used in Ukrainian traditional music.

entries.label: soprano recorder
entries.gloss:
Also known as the descant, it is the third smallest and most common member of the modern recorder family.
Traditionally made of various woods, it is today often made of plastic and used to teach children music.
Not to be confused with the side-blown (concerto) soprano flute.

entries.label: soprano violin
entries.gloss: Tuned a fourth above and about three quarters the size of a standard violin.

entries.label: sordellina
entries.gloss: Starting as a pastoral folk bellows blown bagpipe, it was developed into a complex 2, then 3 and finally 4 chanter with keyed regulators.

entries.label: spike-fiddle
entries.gloss: Particular type of fiddle, long neck, often few strings and usually with a rather small soundbox, it has a spike at the end.

entries.label: spilåpipa
entries.gloss: The spilåpipa is a Swedish fipple flute with eight finger-holes on the top, but no thumb-holes. It has a modal tuning.

entries.label: spinet
entries.gloss: A smaller harpsichord, often with the strings at 30 degrees from the keyboard.

entries.label: spinettone
entries.gloss: Exceptionally long spinet, with multiple strings choirs, its bass-tones were produced by longer, not thicker strings.

entries.label: steel-string acoustic guitar
entries.gloss: Also know and "flat-top", it is a hollow-body acoustic guitar strung with steel strings.

entries.label: stick zither
entries.gloss: Class of instruments where the body is a simple stick with one to many strings attached, may also have up to several usually gourd or wood resonators.

entries.label: string quartet
entries.gloss: Chamber ensemble of four players (two violins, one viola, one cello).

entries.label: string quintet
entries.gloss: Chamber ensemble of five players (two violins, one viola & one cello, then either a second viola, a second cello or a double bass).

entries.label: string synthesizer
entries.gloss: Developed from the 1960's and used mainly in the 70-80's, it was a cheaper and more portable simplification of the mellotron, emulating string ensembles. Its later hybrid development with the electronic organ created "polyphonic ensemble" synthesizers.

entries.label: string trio
entries.gloss: Chamber ensemble of three players (one violin, one viola, one cello).

entries.label: struck idiophone
entries.gloss: Struck idiophone are ones where sound comes from striking the instrument and it as a whole vibrates, without the use of strings or membranes. Therefore these are most often made of sonorous material: metal, wood, glass and even stone.

entries.label: suikinkutsu
entries.gloss: A suikinkutsu is a type of Japanese garden ornament which uses dripping water to create music. Although it is also known as a Japanese water zither, it is named after the sound the koto (a Japanese zither) makes and is not actually a string instrument.

entries.label: suka
entries.gloss: The suka is a once-extinct fiddle from Poland.

entries.label: suling
entries.gloss: Made of bamboo, it has from 4 to 6 finger-holes and a small wedge-shaped fipple. There are many varieties all around Southeast Asia, it is also used in gamelan.

entries.label: suona
entries.gloss: Important to the folk music in northern China, it has a conical wooden body and seven finger holes.

entries.label: surbahar
entries.gloss: Effectively a bass sitar, it has 4 main, 3-4 chikari(drone) and 10-11 resonance strings strung over a wide wooden neck. Made of flat-cut gourd with a possible secondary resonator (tumba) it was invented in 1825 by sitar-player Ghulam Mohammed who wanted a deeper sound.

entries.label: surdo
entries.gloss: The surdo is a large bass drum used in Brazilian music, most notably samba.

entries.label: sursingar
entries.gloss:
Improved further by Jaffar Khan, it had a wooden soundboard, the fingerboard covered with iron and all strings are steel or bronze.
Less common today, it was used for Dhrupad style music.

entries.label: swaragat
entries.gloss: The skin covered deep wooden soundbox, has a neck that is carved like parrot and a gut bridge with three courses of double silk strings, plucked with a horn-plectrum. Used in southern India since ancient times, it is essentially a bass rabab.

entries.label: swarmandal
entries.gloss: Used chiefly in classical Indian songstyles Khyal and Thumri, it has a trapezoid shape with up to 40 metal strings fastened at both sides by iron pegs with one side having tuning keys.

entries.label: syrinx
entries.gloss: Named after the myth of the nymph Syrinx, this reed pan flute was used in ancient Greece.

entries.label: sáo meò
entries.gloss: saó ôi (flute of the Muong)

entries.label: sáo trúc
entries.gloss: The sáo trúc is a Vietnamese transverse flute made of bamboo.

entries.label: säckpipa
entries.gloss: Almost completely disappeared by the 20th century, modern revivals based on museum examples are now used by Swedish folk musicians.

entries.label: sênh tiền
entries.gloss: The sênh tiền is a Vietnamese instrument which is a combination of clappers, a rasp and a jingle, made from three pieces of wood with old Chinese coins attached.

entries.label: t'rưng
entries.gloss: The t'rưng is a bamboo xylophone from the central highlands of Vietnam which is played by ethnic groups such as the Bahnar and the Ê Đê.

entries.label: tabla
entries.gloss: Consists of two drums: the larger baya or dagga for bass and the smaller daya or tabla for rhythm and "melody".

entries.label: tabor
entries.gloss:
Not to be confused with the tambourine.
For the Brazilian frame-drum hit with a whisk see tamborim.
Side drum, often with one or more snares, worn by one person and beaten by one hand, it is often combined with tabor pipes.

entries.label: tack piano
entries.gloss: The tack piano is a permanently altered version of an ordinary piano, which has tacks or nails placed on the felt-padded hammers of the instrument at the point where the hammers hit the strings, giving the instrument a tinny, more percussive sound.

entries.label: taepyeongso
entries.gloss: The taepyeongso is a Korean double reed wind instrument which has a conical wooden body with a metal mouthpiece and cup-shaped metal bell.

entries.label: taiko
entries.gloss: Japanese traditional drum beaten with sticks called bachi.

entries.label: taishogoto
entries.gloss: Developed in the early Taisho period to modernise the ningenkin, it has metal strings and typewriter like keys with a wooden lid over the frets.

entries.label: talharpa
entries.gloss: The talharpa is a four-stringed bowed lyre from northern Europe, mostly played in Estonia.

entries.label: talkbox
entries.gloss: A talkbox is an effects device which enables a musician to modify the sound of an instrument.

entries.label: tamborim
entries.gloss: The tamborim is a small frame drum from Brazil.

entries.label: tambourine
entries.gloss: For the Brazilian frame-drum hit with a whisk see tamborim.

entries.label: tambura
entries.gloss:
Do not confuse with:
  • Serbo-Croat “tamburica” ensemble.
  • Persian/Turkish ancient things that evolved from “tanbur”.
  • Unrelated Indian drone “tanpura”.
  • Related Indian “pandour”.

entries.label: tanbou ka
entries.gloss: Tanbou ka or Tambu ka (a small high-pitched drum).

entries.label: tanbur
entries.gloss: The ancient ancestor of many related lute like instruments.

entries.label: tanpura
entries.gloss: Usually accompanying sitar on ragas, the fretless instrument comes in different sizes: largest; male-voice, smaller; female-voice and smallest; the instrument-accompanying "tanpuri".

entries.label: taonga pūoro
entries.gloss: Traditional musical instruments of the Māori people of New Zealand. Consists of gourds (hue), shell flutes (pu), wooden flutes (koauau), wind roarers and other natural materials.

entries.label: tap dance
entries.gloss: Tap dancing is a type of dance in which the dancer wears special shoes that make a clicking sound as the dancer's feet strike the floor.

entries.label: taphon
entries.gloss: The taphon is a traditional barrel drum from Thailand.

entries.label: tar
entries.gloss: A tar is a single-headed frame drum from North Africa and the Middle East.

entries.label: taragot
entries.gloss: The taragot is a Turkish/Hungarian/Romanian reed instrument related to the saxophone and clarinet.

entries.label: tarota
entries.gloss: Traditional Catalan double reed of medieval origin. Used for cobla music in the 19th century, it mostly disappeared: current tarotas are a modern re-invention.

entries.label: te kū
entries.gloss: also just "kū", a mouthbow with a single string, struck with a light implement of bone or wood.

entries.label: tef
entries.gloss: A Turkish version of tambourine / daf, made from animal skin and played with the fingers.

entries.label: telharmonium
entries.gloss: Considered the first electromechanical musical instrument, an early electronic organ.

entries.label: temür khuur
entries.gloss: Used in folk medicine and shamanistic rituals.

entries.label: tenor banjo
entries.gloss: Used as rhythm accompaniment, it has a shorter neck and 17-19 frets.

entries.label: tenor guitar
entries.gloss: Slightly smaller, four-string version of the steel-string acoustic guitar.

entries.label: tenor trombone
entries.gloss: The tenor trombone is a trombone pitched in B♭.

entries.label: tenor viol
entries.gloss: Tenor member of the viol family.

entries.label: tenor violin
entries.gloss: Tuned an octave below the traditional violin and at about half the size of the cello, it has a range between the cello and the viola. It has a longer neck and thinner ribs than the cello.

entries.label: tenora
entries.gloss: Derived from the tenor shawm, it was independently developed in Catalonia by oboe player Andreu Turon in the 19th century. Made of ginjoler wood with a metal cone, it is used in the traditional cobla and sardana music.

entries.label: theatre organ
entries.gloss: A pipe organ, such as the Wurlitzer, meant to accompany early films.

entries.label: theorbo
entries.gloss: Developed as an extended range bass-lute in Italy during the late sixteenth century, it has an extended neck with a second pegbox.

entries.label: thon
entries.gloss: The thon is a goblet drum with a ceramic or wooden body used in classical Thai and Cambodian music which forms one part of thon and rammana.

entries.label: three-hole pipe
entries.gloss: Ancient pipe originating in Europe, with analogies all over the world, it is often combined with tabor drums.

entries.label: ti bwa
entries.gloss: Percussion instrument from Martinique made of a piece of bamboo laid horizontally and beaten with sticks.

entries.label: tible
entries.gloss: Catalan double-reed, created in the 19th Century by adding valves to the tarota. Used principally for cobla music.

entries.label: timpani
entries.gloss: Timpani (Kettle drum)

entries.label: tin whistle
entries.gloss: Simple six-holed fipple flute, originally made of metal; it used to cost a penny, giving it the alternate name “penny whistle”.

entries.label: tiêu
entries.gloss: The tiêu is a Vietnamese end-blown flute related to the Chinese xiao.

entries.label: tololoche
entries.gloss: The tololoche is a traditional musical instrument from northern Mexico, similar but smaller than the European double bass.

entries.label: tom-tom
entries.gloss: A tom-tom (or just tom) is a cylindrical drum with no snare, commonly found in a standard drum set.

entries.label: topshuur
entries.gloss: The topshuur is a two-stringed lute from Mongolia and Tuva.

entries.label: torupill
entries.gloss: With a bag made of seal's stomach, 5-6 holed chanter of juniper, pine or ash and 1-2 drones, it was attested at least from the 14th century. It survived in coastal regions until its recent revival.

entries.label: traditional basque ensemble
entries.gloss: Instruments used in the traditional music of the Basque people.

entries.label: trautonium
entries.gloss: Electric instrument from the 1930's with a resistor wire and moving metal plate.

entries.label: treble viol
entries.gloss: The treble, descant or soprano member of the viol family.

entries.label: treble violin
entries.gloss: Tuned an octave above and about quarter the size of the traditional violin.

entries.label: triangle
entries.gloss: Tuned metal bar, bent into triangle shape.

entries.label: trikiti
entries.gloss: Diatonic button accordion used in traditional Basque ensemble.

entries.label: tritantri veena
entries.gloss:
Used in India during the medieval period, it had a stick-zither body with 3 strings.
For the the long necked lute called “tritantri veena” in the 19 century, see “sitar”.

entries.label: tromba marina
entries.gloss: A tromba marina is a triangular bowed string instrument used in medieval and Renaissance Europe that consists of a body and neck in the shape of a truncated cone resting on a triangular base.

entries.label: trumpet family
entries.gloss: Family of the brass instrument trumpet.

entries.label: tràm plè
entries.gloss: A variant of the Hmông flute, in which the flute blower’s lips enclose the blowing hole with the vibrating free reed inside.

entries.label: trắng jâu
entries.gloss: trắng jâu bass form of trắng lu

entries.label: trống bông
entries.gloss: The trống bông is a wooden Vietnamese drum with a single drumhead which is played with both hands.

entries.label: tsampouna
entries.gloss:
For the similarly named Italian bagpipe, see zampogna.
Made of goatskin, it has two chanters and no drones. Its name is a reborrowing of the Italian.

entries.label: tube zither
entries.gloss: A zither with a hollow or vaulted body, it can have several resonators.

entries.label: tubon
entries.gloss: Electronic bass organ, proto-keytar.

entries.label: tubular bells
entries.gloss: Larger orchestral version of chimes, closed top hollow metal tubes are set in a stand with a damper operated by pedals, they are tuned at a definite pitch and played with mallets.

entries.label: tubulum
entries.gloss: Invented (or at least made popular) by Blue Man Group, it is made of alternating length PVC pipes and hit with sticks or flaps. It is popular with street musicians.

entries.label: tulum
entries.gloss: Used by shepherds and peoples of the southeast Black Sea region, it is droneless with parallel double chanters each with 5 fingerholes.

entries.label: tumbi
entries.gloss:
For the one string drum-zither also called ektar/ektara, see gopichant.
Used in Punjabi folk and devotional music, it has a single string over a long wooden neck that pierces the tiny parchment covered soundbox.

entries.label: tumutumu
entries.gloss: Made of resonating stone, wood or bone with a striker of stone, bone or hardwood, this ancient instrument was used for rhythm during chanting.

entries.label: tun tuna
entries.gloss:
For the one stringed two spoke drum-zither, see gopichant.
For the one stringed panjabi lute, see tumbi.
Used by among others the Bhil, Kukna and Worli tribes, it has a cylindrical soundbox through which a single metal string is strung between the spoke neck and the bottom membrane.

entries.label: tungso
entries.gloss: Made of thick aged bamboo, this notched end-blown flute may have had a buzzing membrane.

entries.label: turntable
entries.gloss: Used in turntablism, vinyl records are not simply played on it, instead DJ's perform creating sound.

entries.label: txalaparta
entries.gloss: Traditionally consisting of two long wooden planks with corn-husks attached for vibration and hit with long, thick sticks called Makilak, today the planks are shorter and can be made of many other materials like stone, wood or metal and are hit with shorter, lighter sticks.

entries.label: txistu
entries.gloss: Fipple flute that became a symbol for the Basque folk revival.

entries.label: typewriter
entries.gloss: Besides being used for writing, it has also been used in percussion.

entries.label: tōkere
entries.gloss: Castanets of wood, bone, bivalve shells or even flax leaf.

entries.label: udu
entries.gloss: Played ceremonially by Igbo people, it is a clay jug beaten with hands to create sounds.

entries.label: ugal
entries.gloss: Even lower pitched than the pemade , it also has 10 bronze keys suspended over tuned bamboo resonators that the player hits with a small hammer, often in a theatrical manner. It is the leader of the pokok melody.

entries.label: uilleann pipes
entries.gloss: Irish bellow-blown bagpipe

entries.label: ukeke
entries.gloss: The ukeke is a Hawaiian musical bow made of koa wood, 16 to 24 inches long and about 1½ inches wide with two or three strings fastened through and around either end, tuned to an A major triad.

entries.label: ukulele
entries.gloss: The ukulele is a small guitar-like instrument commonly associated with Hawaiian music. It generally has four nylon or gut strings.

entries.label: valiha
entries.gloss: The valiha is a bamboo tube zither from Madagascar.

entries.label: valved brass instruments
entries.gloss: Valved brass instruments use a set of valves which introduce additional tubing into the instrument.

entries.label: veena
entries.gloss:
One of the two subfamilies of Indian chordophones, the South Indian gourd lute used in classical Carnatic music has a single gourd music-box (sometimes a secondary small resonator gourd) with an often hollow neck.
Commonly called just "veena" or "vina", the representative is Saraswati veena, and credits to just "veena" are usually that.

entries.label: venu
entries.gloss: South Indian transverse bamboo flute

entries.label: vertical viola
entries.gloss: Tuned the same as the viola but larger in size, it is played upright like the cello.

entries.label: vessel flute
entries.gloss: A vessel flute is a type of flute with an enclosed rather than cylindrical body.

entries.label: veuze
entries.gloss: Known since atleast the 16th century, it has a long chanter, a three-segmented shoulder drone and a short blowpipe.

entries.label: vibrandoneon
entries.gloss: Wood accordina with piano keys invented in Italy.

entries.label: vichitra veena
entries.gloss: Played like a slide guitar, it has two large gourd resonators with a teak body that often ends in carved peacock heads. Fretless, it has 4 main, 5 chikari and 13 resonance strings, slide is a glass orb named batta.

entries.label: vielle
entries.gloss: Medieval violin

entries.label: vihuela
entries.gloss: Spanish string instrument.

entries.label: viol consort
entries.gloss: Ensemble of multiple instruments of the viol family, usually including at least treble, tenor and bass viols.

entries.label: viol family
entries.gloss: Please use Viola da Gamba with credit "viol" for generic / unspecified viol credits, and not this one. Developed in the 15th century from vihuelists starting to play with bows, viols have frets, flat backs, sloped shoulders, c-holes and are tuned in fourths.

entries.label: viola
entries.gloss:
It is known by many names, based on the full "alto de viola da braccio": "alto", "bratsch (braccio)", "viola", etc.
It is the alto member of the modern violin family and a principal member of the symphony orchestra.

entries.label: viola caipira
entries.gloss: Used in folk-music, It has ten steel strings in five courses.

entries.label: viola d'amore
entries.gloss: While it is fretless and played like the violins "a la braccia", it has a flat back, c-holes and sloping shoulders like a viol. From the baroque period, it has up to 14 strings.

entries.label: viola da gamba
entries.gloss: The generic member of the viol family, use it for "Viol" credits, most viola da gamba credits are however the bass viol.

entries.label: violin
entries.gloss: The most famous member of the violin family, it is actually the "small viol". Its register is soprano and it's a principal member of the symphony orchestra.

entries.label: violin family
entries.gloss:
Developed in the 16th century, these violas da braccio are distinct from the viola da gamba family.
Modern members are:
  • Violin (little viola)
  • Viola
  • Violoncello (small big viola)
  • Double Bass (replacing the violone (big viola))
Past members include the violone (now considered a viol) and bass viol (a forerunner to the violoncello). Occasionally Octobass is also included as a member.

entries.label: violin octet
entries.gloss: New Violin Family of eight proportionally-sized violins developed mainly by Carleen Hutchins, each based directly on the standard violin and its acoustic properties, thus their sound is at a more homogeneous pitch "near the two middle open strings."

entries.label: violino piccolo
entries.gloss: The violino piccolo is a stringed instrument of the baroque period. Most examples are similar to a child's size violin in size and are tuned a third or a fourth higher.

entries.label: viololyra
entries.gloss: Inspired by the violin in 1920, Hellenic luthiers combined parts of the old Cretan lyra with the violin.

entries.label: violoncello piccolo
entries.gloss: Baroque string instrument sized between the viola and cello, it typically has five strings.

entries.label: violone
entries.gloss: Violone, The largest/deepest member of the Viol family.

entries.label: vuvuzela
entries.gloss: Plastic horn often used at football matches in South Africa.

entries.label: walaycho
entries.gloss: Smaller than the charango, it has 10 strings.

entries.label: washboard
entries.gloss: Typical metal ribbed tool used for washing, still in it's wooden frame, often has is additional noisemakers attached, such as cowbell or woodblock. It is played with thimbles as plectrum.

entries.label: washtub bass
entries.gloss: Consisting of a stick, a string and an resonator of various materials, it is used in many countries' low-cost and DIY cultures. It's technically a variable tension chordophone.

entries.label: water drum
entries.gloss: Used ceremonially all over the world, they are clay, wood or metal pots containing water, with an animal hide membrane.

entries.label: whistle
entries.gloss: Simple, single-toned and round-bodied whistle often used for regulation and signalling (sport, traffic, ...).

entries.label: wind chime
entries.gloss:
It differs from other chimes by addition of pendulum(s), such to be worked by wind, the sonorous parts can be rods, bells or other shapes of metal, wood, glass or ceramic.
Often decorated, it is seen as a good luck charm.

entries.label: wind synthesizer
entries.gloss: Wind synthesizer or wind controller, it is connected to a MIDI controller and is played like a wind instrument.

entries.label: wooden fish
entries.gloss: Highly stylised wooden block-bell, it is used in religious ritual. Its prototype, fish board (gyoban) is more obviously shaped like a fish.

entries.label: wot
entries.gloss: Used in Laos and Isan traditional music, it is made of bamboo or ku wood, the individual stopped pipes are arranged around a central core using beeswax.

entries.label: xeremies
entries.gloss:
For the two tube bagless used on Ibiza, see reclam de xeremies.
For the Latin American oboe, see chirimía.
For the mediaeval woodwind, see shawm.
For the Catalan shawm also called xaramita or xirimita, see gralla.

Used historically since the middle ages on the Iberian islands, its bag is made of skin and it has one chanter with usually 3 drones, but of these usually one is real and the others are only decorative.

entries.label: xiao
entries.gloss: Ancient Chinese vertical, end-blown flute made of bamboo.

entries.label: xiaoluo
entries.gloss: The xiaoluo is a Chinese small flat gong whose pitch rises when struck with the side of a flat wooden stick.

entries.label: xun
entries.gloss: The xun is a vessel flute from China which has a blowing hole at the top.

entries.label: xylophone
entries.gloss: Arrangement of struck tuned wooden bars.

entries.label: xylorimba
entries.gloss: Member of the xylophone family, it has 5 octaves.

entries.label: yangqin
entries.gloss: It is related to similar hammered dulcimers in India, middle east and Europe.

entries.label: yatga
entries.gloss: The yatga is a traditional Mongolian plucked zither, similar to the Chinese guzheng.

entries.label: yaylı tanbur
entries.gloss: The yaylı tanbur is a bowed lute from Turkey derived from the older plucked tanbur.

entries.label: yazh
entries.gloss: Used by Dravidian Tamil from at least 2200 years ago, by the 7th century it had come into disuse. It had a curved ebony neck with gut strings above the skin covered resonator shaped like a boat, but there are versions shaped like peacocks, fish and even the monster Makara.

entries.label: yehu
entries.gloss: The yehu is a Chinese bowed string instrument in the huqin family, made from a coconut shell.

entries.label: yonggo
entries.gloss: Used in the traditional Korean music daechwita, it consists of a large two headed wooden barrel painted with dragon designs.

entries.label: yoochin
entries.gloss: Originally introduced to Mongolia from China, it has 13 double wire-strings and a black lacquered wooden soundboard. Traditionally it was only played by townspeople.

entries.label: yu
entries.gloss: From atleast 600 BC, it is made of wood to resemble a tiger with its spine made into notches. Notches are scraped to produce sound, it was used in ensemble with zhu.

entries.label: yueqin
entries.gloss: It has a short fretted neck originally with four silk but now usually nylon or steel strings, and large flat round body, earning it the nickname "moon lute".

entries.label: zabumba
entries.gloss: Brazilian bass drum

entries.label: zampogna
entries.gloss:
For the South-American panpipe, see siku.
For the similarly named Greek bagpipe, see tsampouna.
Made of an entire sheep or goatskin, it has a single round stock that all chanters and drones are fixed into.

entries.label: zarb
entries.gloss: The zarb is a goblet drum from Persia.

entries.label: zhaleika
entries.gloss: Russian single reed hornpipe

entries.label: zhonghu
entries.gloss: The zhonghu is a Chinese bowed string instrument developed from the erhu and tuned a fourth or a fifth lower.

entries.label: zhongruan
entries.gloss: Tenor member of the Chinese ruan family of lutes.

entries.label: zhuihu
entries.gloss: Originating from Henan province, this fretless huqin has the accustomary two strings, but is made of wood.

entries.label: zill
entries.gloss: Known since ancient times in south-east Europe and Turkey, small bronze finger cymbals are used for dancing and other performances. These are similar to the jingles set in some frame drums.

entries.label: çevgen
entries.gloss: Originating in Central Asia, it gained symbolic value to the Turks who used it in Ottoman marching-bands. It is 2-2,5 m long, has a bronze crescent shape with bells and jangles attached.

entries.label: ütőgardon
entries.gloss: Played in folk music of Hungary and Transylvanian regions, its 3-4 strings are plucked or struck with a stick, and its soundbox is made of thick maple, poplar or willow wood.

entries.label: đing buốt
entries.gloss: Ede traditional flute, four finger holes, blowing reed.

entries.label: đàn bầu
entries.gloss: Possibly ancient Vietnamese tube zither. It was originally made of bamboo with one silken string, today it is usually wooden with a metal string. Fastened in one end to a movable device and resonator, the melody comes from changing the string's tension.

entries.label: đàn nguyệt
entries.gloss: The đàn nguyệt or đàn kìm is a two-stringed Vietnamese lute with a long neck and a circular, flat body.

entries.label: đàn nhị
entries.gloss: The đàn nhị is a Vietnamese stringed instrument with a small, cylindrical body, covered at one end with snakeskin. The bow passes between the two strings and the instrument has no frets. This instrument is of Chinese descent but has relatives all over Asia.

entries.label: đàn tam
entries.gloss: The đàn tam is a three-stringed fretless lute from Vietnam.

entries.label: đàn tam thập lục
entries.gloss: Recently imported into Vietnamese instruments, this thirty-six stringed dulcimer has many counterparts in various countries, such as "santoor" in India and "cimbalon" in Europe.

entries.label: đàn tranh
entries.gloss: The đàn tranh is a a long Vietnamese zither with sixteen strings and high, movable bridges. The strings are plucked with plectrums, while the left hand is used for ornamenting the notes by pressing the strings.

entries.label: đàn tứ
entries.gloss: The đàn tứ or đàn đoản is a traditional Vietnamese moon-shaped lute with a short neck.

entries.label: đàn tứ dây
entries.gloss: A latter-day construction in the form of a four-stringed, square-bodied bass guitar.

entries.label: đàn tỳ bà
entries.gloss: The đàn tỳ bà is a four-stringed Vietnamese lute with a pear-shaped body. Like the Chinese pipa from which is derived, it has greatly elevated frets at the neck.

entries.label: ģīga
entries.gloss: The ģīga is a two-stringed bowed zither found in Latvia.

entries.label: ōtsuzumi
entries.gloss: The ōtsuzumi is an hourglass-shaped Japanese drum, larger than the kotsuzumi.

entries.label: šargija
entries.gloss: The šargija is a long necked plucked lute used in the folk music of the Balkans.

entries.label: żafżafa
entries.gloss: The żafżafa or rabbaba is a Maltese friction drum consisting of a container (made of tin, pottery or wood) covered with animal skin with a long Arundo donax reed attached.

entries.label: żaqq
entries.gloss: Made of a whole animal-skin, it is used in festivals. The blowpipe (mserka) is made of rubber or cane, the chanter (saqqafa) are two cane pipes, one 2 holed, the other 5 holed, with the bell of an ox horn.

entries.label: żummara
entries.gloss:
Made of bamboo with one end covered with grease-paper, it is a "side-blown" mirliton.
Not to be confused with the Egyptian/Iraqi zummara which is an instrument similar to a chalumeau.
